# Configuration Reference
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/build/become-a-validator/configuration-reference

Use this as the technical reference for validator configuration. For setup flow, use [Node Setup](/build/become-a-validator/node-setup). For troubleshooting and operator procedures, use [Operations](/build/become-a-validator/operations). For health endpoints and alerts, use [Monitoring](/build/become-a-validator/monitoring).

## config.toml

Copy `config.template.toml` to `config.toml` and fill in your values.

### `[node]`

```toml
[node]
node_id = "oracle-1"        # Unique identifier used in logs
p2p_listen_addr = "0.0.0.0" # Address to listen on for P2P connections
p2p_port = 6690              # TCP port for ragep2p
```

### `[keys]`

Choose one provisioning pattern.

**Option 1 — direct hex**

```toml
[keys]
offchain_private_key = "76918f97bfe8..."

[keys.onchain_private_key]
private_key = "ed6ca3d3ac17..."
```

Use this when you want explicit control over the key material. The offchain key is Ed25519 hex, while the dev/testing onchain key is a secp256k1 private key.

The config encryption key is derived automatically from your offchain key. Do not try to configure it separately in `config.toml`.

**Option 2 — key file**

```toml
[keys]
key_file_path = "./keystore/ocr2_<id>.json"
```

Use this when you want the node to read the OCR2/offchain bundle from disk. The companion P2P identity must live beside it as `./keystore/p2p_<peerID>.json`, so mount the whole `./keystore` directory into the container if you run Docker. Keep both files at `0600` permissions.

**Option 3 — AWS KMS for the onchain key**

```toml
[keys]
offchain_private_key = "76918f97bfe8..."

[keys.onchain_private_key]
kms_key_id = "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789:key/abcd-1234"
```

Use this when you want the offchain/OCR2 identity managed separately from the production onchain signer. Supported KMS identifiers: full ARN, alias, or UUID.

The KMS key must be an asymmetric signing key of type `ECC_SECG_P256K1`. In production, authorize only the validator runtime role to call `kms:Sign`. Keep admin principals able to manage the key, but do not grant them signing rights unless they also operate the validator. This keeps operational administration separate from report-signing authority.

### `[p2p]`

```toml
[p2p]
bootstrap_peers = [
  "12D3KooWGc9hJKBWks3oq9e7H4oZseoncbrxcZQfkW5NTBH473un@bootstrap-1.supervaults.superform.xyz:6690",
  "12D3KooWCDXcCoE86B4dfMg5hXpoPr6xj4wGRaYqxHbkgPZW3yer@bootstrap-2.supervaults.superform.xyz:6690",
]
# announce_addresses = ["203.0.113.42:6690"]
```

Set `announce_addresses` if your node listens on one address but other validators must dial a different public endpoint.

Do not front the P2P port with Cloudflare or any HTTP proxy. ragep2p expects direct TCP reachability.

### `[database]`

```toml
[database]
url = "postgresql://oracle:password@localhost:5432/oracle_db?sslmode=disable"
max_connections = 10
max_idle_conns = 5
conn_max_lifetime = 3600
```

### `[monitoring]`

```toml
[monitoring]
metrics_port = 9090
health_port = 8080
log_level = "info"
log_format = "json"
health_check_interval = "1h"
max_pps_deviation_ppb = 10000000
```

### `[ocr2]`

```toml
[ocr2]
config_version = 3
# config_sync_chain_id = 1
```

`config_sync_chain_id` defaults to Ethereum mainnet (`1`). This is the chain where `SuperGovernor` emits validator config updates, so every node must watch the same source chain.

All nodes must use the same `config_version`. A mismatch produces a different config digest and prevents consensus.

### `chain_config_path`

```toml
chain_config_path = "./chains.yaml"
```

---

## chains.yaml

`chains.yaml` maps chain ID to the chain configuration your node should observe.

```yaml
1:
  name: ethereum
  chain_id: 1
  https_rpc: "https://eth-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_KEY"
  wss_rpc:   "wss://eth-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_KEY"
  block_time: 12s
  supported_strategies:
    - "0xVault1Address"
    - "0xVault2Address"
  ecdsa_oracle_address:   "0x..."
  super_governor_address: "0x..."
```

### Field reference

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `name` | string | Human-readable chain label used in logs and metrics. |
| `chain_id` | integer | EVM chain ID; must match the top-level map key. |
| `https_rpc` | string | HTTPS RPC endpoint for reads and tx submission. |
| `wss_rpc` | string | WebSocket RPC endpoint for event subscriptions. |
| `block_time` | duration | Expected block time in Go duration format. |
| `supported_strategies` | string[] | Vault addresses this node will observe. |
| `ecdsa_oracle_address` | string | `ECDSAPPSOracle` contract address supplied during onboarding. |
| `super_governor_address` | string | `SuperGovernor` contract address supplied during onboarding. |

### RPC requirements

- HTTPS is required on every configured chain.
- WSS is required for event subscriptions.
- Public rate-limited endpoints are not suitable for production.

### Scope rules

Only include chains that Superform assigned to your validator deployment and for which you have reliable RPC access. A broken chain config creates observation errors for every strategy on that chain.

Typical supported deployments include Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, and Polygon, but only configure the chains Superform assigned to your validator.

---

## OCR2 timing presets

The versioned `config/vN.json` files define the OCR2 timing profile. Every validator in the network must use the same version.

### v2 — high-frequency testing

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| `delta_round` | 2s |
| `delta_progress` | 120s |
| `delta_resend` | 30s |
| `delta_grace` | 5s |
| `delta_stage` | 10s |
| `r_max` | 3 |
| `max_stale_duration` | 5m |

### v3 — hourly production default

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| `delta_round` | 30m |
| `delta_progress` | 10m |
| `delta_resend` | 5m |
| `delta_grace` | 1m |
| `delta_stage` | 2m |
| `r_max` | 5 |
| `max_stale_duration` | 5m |

### Freshness controls

| Layer | Config location | Purpose |
|------|------------------|---------|
| Round cadence | `delta_round` | How often the protocol attempts a report |
| Report freshness | `max_stale_duration` | Rejects reports that finalize too late |
| Node health alerting | `health_check_interval` | Warns when no onchain confirmation arrives |
| Contract enforcement | `maxStaleness` | Auto-pauses a strategy if updates stop |

For the production `v3` profile, that contract-side `maxStaleness` window is designed around a 24-hour safety boundary even though rounds attempt far more frequently.

### Switching versions

Update `config_version` on all nodes and restart them in a coordinated window. Mixed versions split the network until every validator converges on the same config digest.

---

# Monitoring
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/build/become-a-validator/monitoring

Use this page when you need validator observability and alerting guidance. For config fields, use [Configuration Reference](/build/become-a-validator/configuration-reference). For operator procedures, use [Operations](/build/become-a-validator/operations).

## Health endpoints

Both ports are configured under `[monitoring]` in `config.toml`.

| Endpoint | Port | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| `GET /metrics` | `metrics_port` | Prometheus scrape target |
| `GET /healthz` | `health_port` | Process + DB liveness |
| `GET /readyz` | `health_port` | Same checks today; reserved for future readiness gates |

Quick check:

```bash
curl -s localhost:8080/healthz
curl -s localhost:8080/readyz
curl -s localhost:9090/metrics | grep ^ocr2_ | head -20
```

## Priority signals

If you only alert on a handful of metrics, start here:

- `ocr2_up` — process liveness
- `ocr2_strategy_last_update_seconds` — confirms PPS updates are still landing onchain
- `ocr2_strategy_update_stale` — fastest signal that a strategy has stopped updating
- `ocr2_transmit_total` labeled by `status` — shows whether transmit attempts are succeeding
- `ocr2_plugin_observations_total` labeled by `result` — reveals RPC or observation failures
- `ocr2_config_version` and `ocr2_config_signers` — confirm the node loaded the expected active network config

## Metrics reference

### Onchain transmission health

- `ocr2_strategy_last_update_seconds` (labels: `chain_id`, `strategy`) — gauge with the Unix timestamp of the latest observed `PPSValidated` event
- `ocr2_strategy_update_stale` (labels: `chain_id`, `strategy`) — gauge set to `1` when no `PPSValidated` event arrives within `health_check_interval`

### Transmitter

- `ocr2_transmit_total` (labels: `chain_id`, `status`) — counter of transmission attempts by outcome
- `ocr2_transmit_strategies_total` (label: `chain_id`) — counter of strategies packed into submitted transactions
- `ocr2_transmit_pack_errors_total` (label: `chain_id`) — counter of report packing failures
- `ocr2_transmit_duration_seconds` (label: `result`) — histogram of end-to-end transmit latency

### Plugin phases

- `ocr2_plugin_phase_duration_seconds` (labels: `phase`, `result`) — histogram of phase latency
- `ocr2_plugin_phase_total` (labels: `phase`, `result`) — counter of phase invocation outcomes
- `ocr2_plugin_observations_total` (labels: `chain_id`, `result`) — counter of per-strategy observation outcomes
- `ocr2_plugin_insufficient_observations_total` (label: `chain_id`) — counter of vaults dropped because quorum observations were not available

## Alerting baseline

For production, alert on the smallest set of signals that prove the node can observe, participate, and transmit:

| Signal | Suggested action |
|--------|------------------|
| `ocr2_up` missing or `0` | Page or notify the operator immediately |
| `ocr2_strategy_update_stale == 1` | Treat as an incident; check RPC, config, and transmission logs |
| `ocr2_transmit_total{status="failure"}` increasing | Investigate transmitter key, RPC health, gas, and contract reverts |
| `ocr2_plugin_observations_total{result="error"}` increasing | Check per-chain RPC health and vault configuration |
| Unexpected `ocr2_config_version` | Confirm the node loaded the intended onchain config |

Email, Slack, or SNS-style notifications are enough for most operators. Operators with SLA requirements should route these alerts into PagerDuty, Opsgenie, or an equivalent on-call system.

## Recommended operating habit

After every config change, restart, or upgrade, verify three things in this order:

1. `/healthz` is healthy
2. `ocr2_config_version` and `ocr2_config_signers` match expectations
3. `ocr2_strategy_last_update_seconds` continues advancing

---

# How It Works
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/build/become-a-validator/how-it-works

This page explains the protocol. It does not repeat setup or runbook instructions. For the rollout model and validator incentives, use [Economics](/build/become-a-validator/economics).

## The problem validators solve

SuperVaults rely on price-per-share (PPS) updates to value positions correctly. A single trusted updater would be a central point of failure. The validator network replaces that with an OCR2 quorum: multiple operators observe PPS independently, agree offchain, and submit one signed report onchain.

## Core components

- **Validator nodes** observe PPS values on assigned chains.
- **OCR2** coordinates offchain consensus.
- **`ECDSAPPSOracle`** accepts quorum-backed PPS reports onchain.
- **`SuperGovernor`** is the source of truth for validator membership and network config.

## OCR2 round flow

A production `v3` deployment attempts a round every 30 minutes.

```text
Leader selected
    │
    ├─ Query        Leader broadcasts round context
    ├─ Observation  Validators fetch PPS independently
    ├─ Report       Leader aggregates observations
    ├─ Finalize     Leader shares the candidate report
    ├─ Accept       Validators validate freshness and safety
    ├─ Sign         Validators sign the finalized report
    └─ Transmit     Designated transmitter posts onchain
```

An epoch is a group of rounds led by the same leader. After `r_max` rounds, or when the leader stalls for longer than `delta_progress`, OCR2 advances to a new epoch and deterministically rotates leadership.

## What your node does

### Observation

Your node calls `pricePerShare()` for each configured strategy, on each configured chain, using the RPC endpoints in `chains.yaml`.

That observation is packaged for OCR2 messaging and signed with your offchain identity before it is shared across the validator mesh.

### Report assembly

If your node is the round leader, it:

1. filters invalid or missing observations
2. requires enough valid observations to satisfy quorum
3. computes the median PPS per vault
4. builds the ABI-encoded report payload

If a vault does not receive enough valid observations, it is dropped from that round instead of poisoning the whole report.

### Acceptance checks

Before signing, every validator checks:

- report freshness against `max_stale_duration`
- optional deviation guard versus its own observation
- whether the onchain nonce changed before acceptance

### Transmission

The designated transmitter submits the report to `ECDSAPPSOracle.transmit()`. If quorum is valid, the contract updates PPS and emits `PPSValidated`.

Onchain verification checks the submitted validator signatures against the registered signer set before the PPS update is accepted.

## Quorum and fault tolerance

The network is configured so it can tolerate a bounded number of faulty validators while still producing correct results.

For OCR2 this is the Byzantine constraint that matters: with `N` validators and fault tolerance `F`, the config must satisfy `F * 3 < N`. In practice Superform chooses an odd quorum so `F = (quorum - 1) / 2`, then builds the validator set around that limit.

| Validators (`N`) | Quorum | Max faulty (`F`) |
|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| 4 | 3 | 1 |
| 7 | 5 | 2 |
| 10 | 7 | 3 |
| 13 | 9 | 4 |

If fewer than `quorum` validators sign a round, that round does not produce an onchain report.

## How validator identity maps into the config

Every validator contributes one aligned identity across three places in the active config:

- `validators[i]` is the Ethereum address derived from that validator's onchain public key
- `validatorPublicKeys[i]` is the 65-byte uncompressed ECDSA public key used for onchain signature verification
- `OracleIdentity[i]` carries the same validator's `validatorPublicKey`, `peerID`, `offchainPublicKey`, and `configEncryptionPublicKey`

Those arrays are not loosely related metadata. They are positional invariants. If the same validator is not represented at the same index across all three, config loading breaks.

## What happens when something breaks

### One validator is offline

Consensus still proceeds as long as the network remains within its fault-tolerance threshold.

### The leader is offline

Other validators wait for `delta_progress`, then a new epoch starts with a new leader.

### Too many validators are unavailable

The network cannot reach quorum. Rounds fail, `PPSValidated` stops advancing, monitoring turns stale, and strategies eventually hit onchain `maxStaleness` protections.

## Config digests

Every node independently derives a config digest from the active validator set, their keys, quorum, and OCR2 timing parameters.

If your digest differs from the rest of the network, the usual causes are:

- mismatched `config_version`
- observing a different `ValidatorConfigSet` event
- running against the wrong deployment inputs

That is an operational issue, not a protocol mystery. Fix the inputs and the digest should converge.

---

# Economics
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/build/become-a-validator/economics

<Warning>
Validator economics are not final yet. Phase 1 is permissioned and does not include the full staking and slashing model described here.
</Warning>

This page covers the validator incentive model and rollout path. For protocol mechanics, use [How It Works](/build/become-a-validator/how-it-works).

## Why validators get paid

Validators provide the PPS updates SuperVaults need to function safely. If updates stop or become dishonest, vault operations degrade quickly. Rewards exist to keep high-quality operators online and aligned with the network.

## Rewards

Vault operators pay upkeep fees in **$UP** for active oracle coverage. Those fees are distributed to participating validators.

The intended model is:

- more stake increases reward weight
- better participation preserves reward eligibility
- missed rounds reduce your effective payout

Exact thresholds and rates are governance parameters and have not been published yet.

## Staking

Phase 2 is expected to require validators to bond **$UP**.

That bond is intended to:

- serve as collateral for slashing
- weight participation and rewards
- enforce a minimum commitment to stay active

## Slashing

Slashing is designed to penalize two categories of failure:

- **misreporting** — signing materially incorrect or invalid PPS data
- **insufficient participation** — staying below required uptime / contribution thresholds

Exact slash sizes and observation windows are still pending.

## Insurance fund

A portion of validator economics is expected to seed an insurance fund intended to backstop depositors if oracle failures cause verified harm.

It is not meant to cover:

- unrelated smart contract bugs
- strategy market losses
- immaterial losses below a governance-defined threshold

## Rollout phases

| Phase | Model | Status |
|-------|-------|--------|
| Phase 1 | Permissioned validator set | Live |
| Phase 2 | Open bonding, slashing, insurance fund seeding | Planned |
| Phase 3 | Governance-managed validator rotation | Planned |

## Practical takeaway for operators

Treat the current program as operationally serious even before the full economic model is live. Phase 1 may be permissioned, but uptime, correctness, and incident response still matter because the vaults depend on your node behaving like production infrastructure.

---

# Operate a SuperVault
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Configure a vault" icon="sliders" href="/operate/quickstart">
    Prepare access, sources, hooks, execution accounts, and funding before activation.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Build strategies" icon="diagram-project" href="/operate/strategy/quickstart">
    Save an inactive strategy, check units and sizing, and test supported behavior.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Operate and investigate" icon="magnifying-glass" href="/operate/ui/intent-history">
    Follow an intent to its transactions and reconcile the resulting positions.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Access and API reference" icon="code" href="/operate/api/overview">
    Distinguish public reads, authenticated browser operations, and service contracts.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## Operating boundaries

Strategy rules decide **when** the offchain engine may publish an intent. Onchain manager checks, hook registration, Merkle proofs, and venue constraints determine **what** a transaction can execute. A disclosed rule is not automatically an onchain restriction.

A saved definition, a published intent, a completed transaction, and the intended economic outcome are separate evidence. See [Concepts](/operate/concepts) for the enforcement layers, [Launch checklist](/operate/ui/setup-checklist) for readiness, and [Playbooks](/operate/playbooks/carry) for portfolio operations.

---

# Operating concepts
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate/concepts

## Enforcement layers

| Layer | Responsibility | What it does not prove |
|---|---|---|
| Strategy Engine | Evaluate offchain rules, sizing, lifecycle, cooldown, and publication gates | A rule is not a contract-level restriction on every authorized manager |
| SuperVault contracts | Share accounting, ERC-7540 redemption flow, manager checks, pricing and fee constraints | A saved engine definition has been executed |
| Hooks and Merkle authorization | Check registered hooks and authorized parameter combinations against applicable roots | The selected action is economically appropriate |
| External venue | Apply its own collateral, debt, liquidity, transfer, and liquidation rules | That an entire planned unwind will complete |
| OMS | Process intents, construct execution, track events and transaction results | A completed record alone proves the target portfolio state |

Vault assets can be idle or deployed into external positions. For carry, the underlying asset, collateral, borrowed token, and yield-source shares are different assets with different units. Do not equate TVL with immediately withdrawable cash.

## Four separate changes

1. **Save a strategy:** an authenticated offchain mutation. Create/Save does not require a hook-root transaction and does not start a newly created strategy.
2. **Authorize hooks:** configure leaves, generate the tree, and update the onchain root through the applicable proposal and timelock. Publishing a downloadable proof artifact is a separate action.
3. **Start execution:** transition the strategy to `RUNNING` only after funding, permission, freshness, and plan checks. A true rule can still be blocked by publication gates.
4. **Reconcile the result:** follow intent, execution, fill, and receipt identifiers; inspect token, share, collateral, and debt changes.

[Lifecycle](/operate/strategy/lifecycle) covers state and concurrency. [Hooks](/operate/ui/merkle-trees) covers authorization.

## Accounting and operational readiness

PPS values shares in the underlying asset. It is not a guaranteed withdrawal quote or a promise of immediate liquidity. PPS freshness and validator acceptance matter independently of source price and position-data freshness. Performance fee skims can reduce PPS; see [Economics](/learn/supervaults/economics).

UP upkeep funds the protocol's upkeep system. Native-chain gas funds transaction submission. Depositor capital funds positions and redemption liquidity. None substitutes for the other two. See [Upkeep and gas funding](/operate/ui/funding).

## Access is not signing authority

A browser session identifies a user; a vault role authorizes particular requests. A wallet signature or delegated session authorizes a particular onchain action. A public dashboard, assigned view-only access, a manager role, and an executor session are not interchangeable. The [permissions matrix](/operate/permissions) separates these checks.

---

# Prerequisites and access
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate/prerequisites

## Access checklist

- Open [SuperformOS](https://os.superform.xyz). Public discovery does not require manager access.
- For Operate, use **Connect**, complete the shared account flow, and accept the Superform terms if prompted. The user must review and accept terms themselves.
- Obtain a role for the exact **chain and vault address**. Primary and Secondary Managers can author strategies. Assigned view-only users can inspect rules but cannot save strategies or run simulations.
- Prepare the authorized transaction-signing wallet, and native gas on the target chain. Connecting a different wallet does not transfer a vault role.
- For a new vault, prepare the underlying token address and decimals, provider metadata, managers, fee recipient, and fee/timing configuration.

A private demonstration needs an explicitly authorized, isolated vault and inactive strategies. Base is a production network, not a sandbox.

## Configuration checklist

| Input | Check before use |
|---|---|
| Chain and vault | Use the selected network and deployed address, not a name-only search |
| Underlying asset | Verify token identity and precision; do not assume all SuperVaults use the same decimals |
| Source and oracle | Confirm the source's assets, shares, pricing denomination, freshness, and withdrawal limits |
| Hook plan | Confirm every target and parameter combination is authorized |
| Executor | Confirm manager membership and a valid delegated session |
| Funding | Check UP upkeep, execution gas, and strategy input balances separately |

Use the application's supported network choices and [Deployment Addresses](/deployment-addresses); network availability is not permission to reuse another chain's source or oracle configuration.

## Supported access paths

[Authentication](/operate/authentication) explains the browser session. [API boundaries](/operate/api/overview) identifies public reads and upstream service contracts. A documented service path is not a promise of public automation credentials. Arrange approved programmatic access with the Superform team before building a writer.

The [launch sequence](/operate/quickstart) leads to one [readiness checklist](/operate/ui/setup-checklist). Strategy authoring starts separately at [Build your first strategy](/operate/strategy/quickstart).

---

# Access and roles
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate/permissions

## Role boundaries

| Role | Scope |
|---|---|
| Primary Manager | Onchain main manager; primary-only configuration and delegation |
| Secondary Manager | Delegated onchain manager; operational actions within protocol constraints |
| View-only | Offchain vault assignment; authenticated inspection, not execution |
| Registry maintainer | Global metadata maintenance; not automatically a vault manager |
| Executor/session key | Delegated execution authority with explicit validity and scope |

Manager authority does not bypass hook proofs, venue checks, fee limits, pricing constraints, or timelocks. Assets may be held in external positions, not only idle in the vault.

## Operation matrix

The table distinguishes the inspected application/API policy from contract authority. A UI control can be narrower than an API policy; API preparation is not permission to sign as another account.

| Operation | Application or API gate | Transaction boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Inspect public dashboard and allowed history | Public vault and anonymous read allowlist | None |
| Open **View rules** in Operate | Assigned view-only, Primary, or Secondary Manager | None |
| Create/save/reorder/start strategies; run simulation | Primary or Secondary Manager for the selected vault | Offchain mutation; starting can cause later execution |
| Add/remove Secondary Manager | Erebor prepare endpoints: Primary Manager | Aggregator `addSecondaryManager` / `removeSecondaryManager`: main manager |
| Add/remove view-only user; update display name | Erebor: either manager | Offchain mutation |
| Whitelist/remove sources or change paired oracle | Yield Sources UI: Primary Manager; Erebor prepare endpoints: either manager | Check the prepared contract call and signing authority |
| Create/activate hook config; request tree generation | Erebor: either manager | Offchain until root update |
| Propose strategy hook root | Main manager | Signed proposal; execution waits for configured timelock |
| Request proof artifact publication | Erebor: Primary Manager | Artifact publication is separate from root activation |
| Change fee configuration, PPS expiration, deviation threshold, or banned leaves | Erebor settings writes: Primary Manager | Prepared onchain calls; proposal/execute where applicable |
| Propose/cancel minimum PPS update interval | Erebor: Primary Manager | Signed proposal/cancellation |
| Execute matured minimum PPS update interval | Erebor execution preparation: either manager | Contract execution is permissionless after a valid pending proposal's timelock expires |
| Set/delete redemption timing setting | Erebor: Primary Manager | Offchain setting, not a transaction prepare call |
| Prepare Erebor session grant/revoke | Primary Manager | Delegation transaction still requires the authorized signer |
| Pause/unpause vault | Erebor prepare: either manager | Aggregator pause/unpause: either manager |
| Pause/resume per-vault keeper services | Erebor: either manager | Offchain service control |
| Create/attach/detach vault notification channels | Erebor: either manager | Offchain configuration |
| Propose upkeep withdrawal | Primary Manager | Timelocked withdrawal; inspect recipient and execution conditions |

OMS grant/rotation preparation has a separate BFF manager gate and contract signing requirements. Do not infer that access to prepared calldata makes a Secondary Manager eligible to sign every delegated-session change. See [Execution accounts](/operate/ui/execution-accounts).

## Primary Manager replacement

The current Aggregator has two different paths:

- `changePrimaryManager`: privileged `SUPER_GOVERNOR` path.
- `proposeChangePrimaryManager`: a Secondary Manager proposes a replacement and fee recipient; `executeChangePrimaryManager` applies it after the manager-change timelock and contract checks.

The ordinary User Management tab displays the Primary Manager; it is not a replacement wizard. Replacement is neither an unrestricted Secondary Manager edit nor governance-only. Review pending proposals, effective time, and the contract's reset of delegated configuration before using an approved recovery procedure.

## Verification boundary

These gates were checked against application, Erebor policy, and Aggregator source. They do not certify the deployed bytecode or a successful authenticated signing rehearsal. For any mutation, verify the selected vault, current role, prepared call, resulting receipt if applicable, and a fresh readback. [Authentication](/operate/authentication) covers session failures; [User Management](/operate/ui/user-management) covers assignments.

---

# Find and select a vault
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate/ui/home

## Public discovery

[SuperformOS](https://os.superform.xyz) provides public vault discovery and read-only detail pages. Discovery is filtered by activation and visibility policy; it is not an inventory of every deployed contract. A missing list entry does not prove that a vault does not exist.

Select a vault by chain and address. Public detail uses `/supervaults/{chain_name}/{vaultAddress}` and exposes Dashboard, Strategy, Intent History, Hooks, Yield Sources, Roles, and Vault Settings views where public data is available. Manager controls remain in Operate. Public Strategy cards do not grant access to the authenticated rule editor.

## My SuperVaults

After [connecting](/operate/authentication), open **Operate → My SuperVaults**. This list is scoped to your assigned vault roles. If a vault is missing, check the connected account, chain, address, and role assignment before creating another vault.

The selected vault determines the context for Setup, Dashboard, Strategy, Simulation, Intent History, Hooks, Yield Sources, User Management, Vault Settings, Keepers, and Pause. Recheck this context before saving a definition or signing a transaction.

| Task | Surface |
|---|---|
| Browse public vault data | Public discovery and vault detail |
| Inspect assigned private rules | Operate with view-only or manager role |
| Change configuration | Operate with the operation-specific manager role |
| Deploy a new vault | **Create a SuperVault**, `/operate/create` |
| Review listing availability | **Distribute**, `/distribute` |

[Launch sequence](/operate/quickstart) covers setup; [Access and roles](/operate/permissions) defines permissions. Do not use a visible public route as evidence of authenticated access or execution readiness.

---

# Launch sequence
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate/quickstart

<Steps>
<Step title="Create or select the vault">
Open **Operate → My SuperVaults** and verify the chain and address. For a new vault, use **Create a SuperVault** at `/operate/create`. Review identity, managers, fees, and metadata; sign only the intended deployment, then wait for indexing. [Create a vault](/operate/ui/create-vault) describes the transaction and recovery path.
</Step>
<Step title="Prepare sources and pricing">
In **Yield Sources**, select the intended source and compatible oracle, review asset/share units and pricing, then complete the whitelist transaction. A source must exist before hook parameters and strategy plans can refer to it. See [Yield sources and pricing](/operate/ui/yield-sources).
</Step>
<Step title="Authorize hooks">
Open **Hooks**. Save and activate the intended configuration version, generate its tree, and compare it with the current onchain root. The Primary Manager proposes the strategy root; after the configured timelock, execute the update and verify it. Publish the matching proof artifact separately. See [Hooks and authorization](/operate/ui/merkle-trees).
</Step>
<Step title="Prepare execution and funding">
Check the executor's manager status and session validity in [Execution accounts](/operate/ui/execution-accounts). Fund [UP upkeep and native gas](/operate/ui/funding) independently. A hook count, strategy count, or active flag does not prove an executable plan.
</Step>
<Step title="Save and test an inactive strategy">
Follow [Build your first strategy](/operate/strategy/quickstart). Read back the saved definition, version, and inactive lifecycle state. Check expressions, units, and plan fixtures; use [Simulation](/operate/ui/simulation) only for admitted inputs and modeled actions. Do not start production automation to test an editor.
</Step>
<Step title="Review launch evidence">
Use the [Launch checklist](/operate/ui/setup-checklist) to reconcile deployment, authorization, execution readiness, and distribution. Activation of an approved strategy and public listing are separate decisions. Private testing does not require a public listing. Monitor actual runs through [Intent History](/operate/ui/intent-history) and [Positions and accounting](/operate/ui/dashboard).
</Step>
</Steps>

---

# Launch checklist
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate/ui/setup-checklist

## Setup rows

Open **Setup** with the intended chain and vault selected. The visible checklist summarizes configuration; it does not preflight every executable plan.

| Row | Evidence represented | Additional launch check |
|---|---|---|
| **Vault is created** | Indexed deployment exists | Verify chain, underlying, vault, and strategy addresses |
| **Upkeep is staked** | Reported activation state | Inspect actual balance, required threshold, and shortfall |
| **Hooks are set up** | At least one hook in the active config | Verify all plan leaves, generated root, onchain sync, and available proofs |
| **Yield sources are set up** | A source is whitelisted | Verify each intended source, oracle, unit scale, freshness, and liquidity |
| **Strategy is set up** | A strategy exists | Inspect definition/version, intended state, sizing, priority, cooldown, and concurrency |
| **Vault is live on Superform** | Distribution visibility/availability | Verify allocator-facing listing and redemption path before routing public deposits |

The displayed order is not a dependency scheduler. Configure source targets before authoring hooks and plans that reference them. An inactive saved strategy can satisfy an existence check without being approved to run.

## Execution readiness

- [Execution account](/operate/ui/execution-accounts): executor is an authorized manager, session is valid, and rotation is not incomplete.
- [Funding](/operate/ui/funding): UP upkeep, native execution gas, and strategy input assets are independently sufficient.
- [Hooks](/operate/ui/merkle-trees): intended configuration and onchain root agree; every plan step has usable authorization.
- [Strategy tests](/operate/ui/simulation): expressions and denominations have been checked; model limits are recorded. A model run is not a transaction preflight.
- [Operational state](/operate/ui/pause): no unintended vault pause, keeper pause, kill switch, or target emergency lock.
- [Monitoring](/operate/automation/monitoring): stale or unavailable observations raise an alert rather than becoming healthy defaults.

## Activation fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `activation.is_active` | Management service's activation decision |
| `activation.is_discoverable` | Eligibility for public discovery |
| `activation.status` / `activation.reason` | Reported state and optional explanation |
| `upkeep_info.balance` | Raw UP upkeep balance |
| `upkeep_info.threshold.required_balance` | Raw required balance for this chain/vault |
| `upkeep_info.threshold.shortfall` | Raw amount missing from the threshold; zero means sufficient |

Read current thresholds rather than hardcoding a chain minimum. The management implementation supports activation exemptions, so an active flag and positive shortfall are not necessarily contradictory. An exemption is not proof of funded gas, fresh PPS, or a working strategy. Investigate the balance and effective policy before changing funds.

## Private readiness versus public launch

A deployed, role-accessible vault can be prepared and tested privately. It need not be listed to author inactive strategies. Public launch adds distribution metadata, visibility, availability, and an approved depositor operating path. See [Distribution](/operate/ui/distribute).

If Setup and a detailed read disagree, inspect the underlying contract/API state and its freshness. Do not declare readiness from a green summary row alone.

---

# Create Vault
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate/ui/create-vault

Open **Create a SuperVault** at `/operate/create`. Deployment and distribution metadata are separate parts of creation:



1. Editable configuration before anything is signed.
2. Operational setup after the vault exists onchain.

## Before You Start

You need:

- A connected wallet with permission to create and manage the vault.
- The underlying token available in the token registry, or enough metadata to register it.
- An approved provider record for the vault's listing metadata.
- The primary manager wallet that will administer vault-level settings within protocol constraints.
- Fee recipient and fee parameters.

## Editable Wizard Steps

The wizard has four editable steps. You can move back through these steps until you enter the transaction phase.

### 1. Basic Information

Basic Information contains chain, asset, identity, and listing fields.

Configure:

- **Chain** — the deployment network. This is permanent after deployment.
- **Provider** — the approved managed provider associated with the vault.
- **Underlying asset** — the token users deposit into the vault. You can select a registered token or register a custom token.
- **Distribution metadata** — friendly name, description, category, and provider IDs used by Superform distribution surfaces.
- **Onchain identity** — name and symbol. By default these are computed from provider + asset, with an optional manual override.

<Note>
The onchain vault name and symbol are protocol identity. The friendly name, category, provider IDs, and description are distribution metadata used by Superform surfaces.
</Note>

### 2. Managers

Set the primary manager and optional secondary managers.

- The **primary manager** administers vault settings, user management, session keys, and emergency authority within protocol constraints.
- **Secondary managers** can execute delegated vault operations but cannot bypass primary-only settings, Merkle validation, timelocks, or vault accounting.

For production vaults, use a hardware-backed wallet or multisig as the primary manager.

### 3. Fees

Configure:

- Performance fee.
- Management fee.
- Fee recipient.
- PPS timing parameters.
- Optional redeem timelock.

Fee bounds and protocol constraints are read from protocol configuration. The dashboard prepares valid calldata; your wallet signs the resulting transaction.

### 4. Review

Review everything before entering the transaction phase:

- Chain and underlying asset.
- Provider and distribution metadata.
- Onchain name and symbol.
- Managers.
- Fees and timing parameters.

After this point, the wizard moves into signing, indexing, activation, and post-create setup.

## Transaction, Indexing, and Activation

### Sign the Creation Transaction

The dashboard calls Erebor to prepare calldata:

```bash
POST /api/v1/vaults/create/prepare
```

Your wallet signs and submits the transaction onchain. Erebor does not execute the transaction for you.

### Confirm and Index

After the transaction is broadcast, the dashboard confirms the hash:

```bash
POST /api/v1/vaults/create/confirm
```

Erebor creates an indexing job and the UI polls:

```bash
GET /api/v1/vaults/create/jobs/{job_id}
```

Statuses are `pending`, `running`, `completed`, or `failed`.

During indexing, the dashboard also submits distribution metadata when the vault address is resolved. If submission fails, the vault can still exist onchain; confirm availability from the Distribute surface.

<Warning>
`409 Conflict` on confirm means a creation job already exists for that transaction hash. Check the existing job before retrying.
</Warning>

### Activate With Upkeep

After indexing, open **Vault Settings → Upkeep**. Read the balance, threshold, shortfall, and activation decision. Upkeep is distinct from execution gas; an activation exemption can affect the reported state. See [Upkeep and gas funding](/operate/ui/funding).

### Set Up Yield Sources

Creation can continue into yield-source setup. Add at least one whitelisted source and paired oracle before creating strategies or routing deposits.

### Complete or Finish Later

The vault can exist before all setup rows are complete. If you leave the wizard after deployment, use [Setup Checklist](/operate/ui/setup-checklist) to resume activation, hooks, yield sources, strategy, and distribution work.

## Post-Create Setup

Once the vault is indexed, follow the [Launch sequence](/operate/quickstart) and [Launch checklist](/operate/ui/setup-checklist). Configure sources before the hooks and strategy plans that reference them. Verify execution accounts and gas independently of upkeep. Save and read back an inactive strategy before testing; public listing is a separate decision.

## API Reference

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/v1/registry/token-assets` | GET | Browse registered token assets |
| `/api/v1/registry/token-assets` | PUT | Register or upsert a custom token |
| `/api/v1/vaults/create/prepare` | POST | Prepare creation calldata |
| `/api/v1/vaults/create/confirm` | POST | Confirm creation transaction hash |
| `/api/v1/vaults/create/jobs/{id}` | GET | Poll indexing job status |

### PrepareCreateVaultRequest

The following is an illustrative field map, not an executable request. Replace every abbreviated address with independently verified configuration and use the current UI-generated request. No deployment or signing is implied by this example.

```json
{
  "chain_id": 8453,
  "asset": "0xUSDC...",
  "name": "Provider USDC SuperVault",
  "symbol": "proUSDC",
  "main_manager": "0xPrimaryManager...",
  "secondary_managers": [],
  "min_update_interval": 3600,
  "max_staleness": 86400,
  "fee_config": {
    "performance_fee_bps": 1000,
    "management_fee_bps": 200,
    "recipient": "0xFeeRecipient..."
  }
}
```

### ConfirmCreateVaultRequest

Illustrative field map only. Use the actual transaction hash and chain from the deployment, then read back the indexing job and deployed addresses.

```json
{
  "tx_hash": "0xabc...",
  "chain_id": 8453,
  "vault_config": {
    "redeem_timelock_seconds": 0
  }
}
```

# Yield sources and pricing
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate/ui/yield-sources

Yield Source Management controls where a SuperVault is allowed to deploy capital. Each source is a protocol position, such as an ERC-4626 vault or Pendle PT, paired with an oracle that prices the position back into the vault's underlying asset.

Public detail pages expose Yield Sources as a read-only tab. All whitelist mutations happen in the authenticated Operate surface and use the prepare pattern: Erebor prepares calldata and the manager wallet signs the transaction.

## Page Layout

- **Whitelisted Yield Sources** — sources currently enabled for the selected vault.
- **Yield Source Registry** — global source catalog filtered by chain and active status.
- **Oracle Registry** — compatible pricing sources.

Registry entries can include provider data imported from external provider URLs, such as Morpho or Pendle metadata.

## Add a Yield Source

1. Select a registry yield source.
2. Select a compatible oracle.
3. Prepare the add transaction.
4. Sign with the manager wallet.
5. Confirm the source appears in the whitelisted table.

```bash
POST /api/v1/yield-sources/prepare-add
POST /api/v1/yield-sources/prepare-bulk-add
```

Adding a source also keeps the paired emergency-exit strategy lifecycle in sync. The app provisions one `EMERGENCY_EXIT` withdrawal strategy for the source when the active hook and proof prerequisites are available.

## Remove a Yield Source

```bash
POST /api/v1/yield-sources/prepare-remove
POST /api/v1/yield-sources/prepare-bulk-remove
```

Before removing, confirm the vault has no deployed liquidity in the source.

<Warning>
Removing a yield source does not unwind assets. Withdraw first, or use [Pause Operations](/operate/ui/pause) to arm an emergency drain when the situation requires immediate exit.
</Warning>

When a whitelisted source is removed, the paired `EMERGENCY_EXIT` strategy is archived. If an emergency lock is active for that source, removal is blocked until the operator stops the drain.

## Update Oracle

Use oracle updates when the current oracle is wrong, deprecated, or needs a safer pricing path.

```bash
POST /api/v1/yield-sources/prepare-update-oracle
POST /api/v1/yield-sources/prepare-bulk-update-oracle
```

## Source and Oracle Types

These are registry types, not execution-plan target enums. A plan uses canonical values such as `ERC4626` or `VAULT`; do not copy a registry type into a plan without checking the schema.

| Type | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `erc4626` | Standard tokenized vault position |
| `pendle_pt` | Pendle principal token position |
| `erc4626` oracle | Prices by share value |
| `pendle_pt` oracle | Prices by PT market value |
| `pendle_pt_amortized` oracle | Amortizes PT value toward maturity |

## API Reference

Paths below are upstream contracts used through the authenticated browser BFF. The Yield Sources UI uses a Primary Manager gate; Erebor permits either manager to prepare whitelist changes. Check [Access and roles](/operate/permissions), the selected wallet, and the actual prepared call. A broader API preparation policy does not override contract signing authority.

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/v1/yield-sources/{chain_id}/{vault_address}` | GET | Whitelisted sources for a vault |
| `/api/v1/registry/yield-sources` | GET | Browse active registry sources for selection |
| `/api/v1/registry/oracles` | GET | Browse compatible oracles for selection |
| `/api/v1/yield-sources/prepare-add` | POST | Prepare add transaction |
| `/api/v1/yield-sources/prepare-remove` | POST | Prepare remove transaction |
| `/api/v1/yield-sources/prepare-update-oracle` | POST | Prepare oracle update transaction |
| `/api/v1/yield-sources/prepare-bulk-add` | POST | Prepare bulk add transaction |
| `/api/v1/yield-sources/prepare-bulk-remove` | POST | Prepare bulk remove transaction |
| `/api/v1/yield-sources/prepare-bulk-update-oracle` | POST | Prepare bulk oracle update transaction |

## Carry and liquidity checks

Before a source is used in a carry plan, record its asset address/decimals, share address/decimals, PPS convention, price reference, and exit-liquidity observation. A quoted share value does not imply that the whole balance can be redeemed now.

For a borrowing position, also verify chain, Spoke, reserve IDs, collateral/debt tokens, and the position identifier. A registry source and oracle do not by themselves provision a complete borrow→deposit or redeem→repay plan.

Inspect observation timestamps and source availability. Missing or stale risk/price/liquidity data is not zero risk. Use [Variables and units](/operate/strategy/variables) for raw scales and [Carry](/operate/playbooks/carry) for the position mapping. Confirm removal does not strand collateral, debt, shares, or pending redemptions; an empty displayed allocation is not a substitute for reconciliation.

---

# Hooks and authorization
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate/ui/merkle-trees

Open **Hooks** in Operate. The route retains the name `/merkle-trees`. Hook registration, applicable Merkle proofs, and contract checks authorize execution; offchain trigger rules are a separate policy layer.

Public SuperVault detail pages expose hook and proof context as read-only inspection tabs. Drafting, activating, generating, syncing, and publishing remain manager workflows in Operate.

The operational flow is:

1. Draft a root configuration.
2. Activate the configuration version.
3. Generate a merkle tree from the active config.
4. Primary Manager proposes the root, waits for the configured timelock, then the update is executed onchain.
5. Publish the proof artifact for consumers.

## Hook Configs

Hook configs define which hook + parameter combinations the vault authorizes.

When creating a config, choose hooks from the registry and set inspect parameters such as:

- `yield_source` — target yield source address.
- `token` — token address.
- `oracle` — oracle address.
- Freeform hook parameters.

Each parameterized row becomes a merkle leaf. Keepers must supply the matching proof at execution time.

## Activate Config

Only one config version is active at a time. Activating a config selects the version used for the next tree generation.

Activating a config does not update the onchain root by itself. It selects what Erebor will generate next.

## Generate Tree

Generation is asynchronous:

```bash
POST /api/v1/merkle/generate
GET /api/v1/merkle/jobs/{job_id}
```

A `409 Conflict` means generation is already in progress for the vault.

The generated tree includes:

- Root hash.
- Leaf count.
- Config hash / version.
- Leaf details and proof paths.

## Sync Root Onchain

The Sync action compares generated tree state to onchain state and returns the next action:

| Action | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `in_sync` | Onchain root already matches |
| `needs_generation` | Generate a tree for the active config |
| `propose` | Sign a root proposal transaction |
| `pending_timelock` | Wait for the proposal timelock |
| `execute` | Sign execution after timelock expiry |

```bash
GET /api/v1/merkle/sync?vault_address={addr}&chain_id={id}
```

<Warning>
Strategies and emergency exits depend on active merkle withdrawal hooks. A yield source can be whitelisted but still unavailable for execution if the active merkle root does not authorize the required hook path.
</Warning>

## Publish Proof Artifact

Publishing makes the active proof set available to integrators, keepers, and frontends without Erebor authentication. The app exposes this as a primary-manager-gated **Publish** or **Re-publish** action on the active tree. Once the current artifact matches the active tree, the button state becomes **Published**.

```bash
POST /api/v1/merkle/publish
GET /api/v1/merkle/publish/jobs/{id}
GET /api/v1/merkle/published/{chain_id}/{vault}
```

Publishing is separate from syncing. Sync updates the protocol root; publish exposes the proof artifact. A published response includes:

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `published` | Whether a published tree exists for the vault. |
| `published_at` | Timestamp for the most recent publish. |
| `root_hash` | Published merkle root. Verify this against the onchain root before using proofs. |
| `s3_url` | Public JSON artifact containing the full tree and leaf proofs. |
| `total_leaves` | Number of authorized leaf combinations. |
| `tree_id` | Published tree identifier. |
| `is_stale` | Whether the artifact no longer matches the current active tree. |

When `is_stale` is true, re-publish before relying on the artifact for execution. Even when `is_stale` is false, verify `root_hash` against the onchain SuperVaultAggregator state; offchain publish and onchain root sync are independent steps.

An unpublished public artifact does not prove that the onchain root is absent. Conversely, `published: true` does not establish that its root is the root currently accepted by the contract. Compare configuration version, generated tree, published artifact, and contract state separately.

Compact definition discovery and mapped onchain-version history are additional management API reads, not replacements for proofs. Pin the returned tree/version when paginating definitions. An executed root without a completed local generation can be absent from mapped history. See [Management API](/operate/api/erebor#merkle-authorization).

## Emergency Exit Dependency

Emergency liquidity exit requires an active withdrawal hook for the target yield source. If the active config has no matching withdrawal hook or the proof artifact is missing the leaf, the Pause page cannot arm that source until the merkle configuration is fixed.

## API Reference

These are upstream management paths, not a promise of direct anonymous access to every endpoint. The browser uses `/api/erebor`; [API boundaries](/operate/api/overview) and [Access and roles](/operate/permissions) identify the authentication and role checks. Config creation, activation, and generation permit either manager; proof publication requires the Primary Manager.

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/v1/merkle/configs/versions` | GET | Config version history |
| `/api/v1/merkle/configs/version` | GET | Single version by number |
| `/api/v1/merkle/configs/active` | GET | Active config |
| `/api/v1/merkle/configs` | POST | Create new config |
| `/api/v1/merkle/configs/activate` | PUT | Activate a version |
| `/api/v1/merkle/trees` | GET | List trees for a vault |
| `/api/v1/merkle/proofs` | GET | List proofs |
| `/api/v1/merkle/proofs/lookup` | GET | Lookup one proof |
| `/api/v1/merkle/generate` | POST | Start generation |
| `/api/v1/merkle/jobs/{id}` | GET | Poll generation job |
| `/api/v1/merkle/sync` | GET | Determine root sync action |
| `/api/v1/merkle/publish` | POST | Publish active tree proof artifact |
| `/api/v1/merkle/publish/jobs/{id}` | GET | Poll publish job |
| `/api/v1/merkle/published/{chain_id}/{vault}` | GET | Public published tree metadata |

# Execution accounts and session keys
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate/ui/execution-accounts

## Identities to check

| Identity | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Connected manager wallet | Authorizes configuration and signs permitted delegation transactions |
| SuperVault strategy contract | Holds the strategy's onchain execution context |
| Executor address | Must have the required manager authority for this vault |
| Session signer | Time-bound delegated signing identity used by automation |

A browser login is not a session-key grant. An executor address is not a deposit destination. Do not send assets to a signer or an infrastructure key identifier based on its appearance in a response.

## Readiness

The manager Strategy view can show **Set up vault automation** before the canvas is usable. The gate distinguishes missing signing setup, missing executor permissions, invalid session, and an in-progress renewal. A transport error such as **Couldn't load automation status** is unknown readiness, not proof that a grant is missing.

The OMS readiness response includes:

| Field | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| `vault_id`, `chain_id`, `supervault_address`, `strategy_address` | Confirm the exact vault and execution context |
| `executor_address`, `executor_is_manager` | Confirm the executor and its onchain manager membership |
| `primary_kms_alias_present` | Signing configuration exists; not sufficient by itself |
| `primary_session_valid`, `primary_session_expiry` | Current session validity and expiry |
| `has_pending_rotation` | Renewal is in progress; inspect pending state before preparing another grant |
| `ready` | Aggregate readiness result, not proof of hook authorization, gas, liquidity, or a successful plan |

Treat infrastructure key metadata as confidential. Do not copy raw readiness or rotation responses into public tickets, screenshots, or documentation.

## First-time setup

1. Confirm the selected chain, vault, manager wallet, and approved execution scope.
2. Choose **Continue** on **Set up vault automation**. Review **Understand the commitment** and the optional **Session length**.
3. At **Authorize from your wallet**, inspect each prepared transaction's recipient, decoded call, executor, signer, and expiry. A prepare response can include multiple transactions.
4. Use **Approve in wallet** only for the intended calls. Complete them in the displayed order and wait for confirmation.
5. Use **Refresh status** and read readiness again. Submission or a success toast alone is not completion.

The application can prepare calls for a manager but the contract determines which wallet may execute each call. Erebor's session grant/revoke preparation is Primary-Manager-only; OMS preparation and browser access are separate gates. See [Access and roles](/operate/permissions).

## Renewal and revocation

When **Session renewal in progress** appears, use **Continue session renewal** rather than first-time setup. Inspect current and pending signer state and follow the renewal flow's revoke/grant sequence. Complete rotation only after the required transactions have mined and readiness can be reconciled.

For revocation, inspect the current session being revoked, sign with the authorized wallet, wait for its receipt, and read readiness back. Revocation prevents future use of that authority; it does not reverse mined actions or guarantee cancellation of transactions already submitted.

## Failure handling

| Observation | Response |
|---|---|
| Readiness request fails | Check session, service reachability, and vault role; do not repeatedly prepare new keys |
| Executor is not a manager | Review the intended executor and authorized manager-assignment transaction |
| Session expired or invalid | Review renewal state and prepare the appropriate grant/renewal path |
| Transactions confirmed but UI remains gated | Refresh readiness; preserve transaction hashes and investigate indexing or service errors |
| Pending rotation exists | Resume or explicitly cancel that flow; do not assume missing optional metadata means no pending rotation |
| Ready but intents fail | Check [gas funding](/operate/ui/funding), proofs, inputs, and [execution diagnostics](/operate/strategy/troubleshooting) |

The [OMS API reference](/operate/api/oms) lists the upstream contracts. These procedures are source-backed operating guidance, not evidence of a deployed authenticated rehearsal.

---

# Upkeep and gas funding
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate/ui/funding

## Three balances

| Balance | Pays for | Does not replace |
|---|---|---|
| UP upkeep | Protocol upkeep and activation policy | Native-chain gas or strategy input assets |
| Native execution gas | Transactions from the configured submitting account | UP upkeep or a valid session grant |
| Vault/position assets | Deposits, repayments, reserves, and redemption liquidity | Execution gas or keeper authorization |

A funded manager wallet may pay for setup signatures while the automation execution path uses a different submitting account. Verify that account and chain with the authorized deployment configuration. Do not derive a funding address from a display name, KMS identifier, or session signer field.

## Fund upkeep

1. Open **Vault Settings → Upkeep** for the intended vault.
2. Read the upkeep token, raw balance, `threshold.required_balance`, and `threshold.shortfall`. Use the token's decimals for display and input conversion.
3. Review the token allowance and prepared deposit amount, recipient, and chain. Sign the intended approval/deposit transactions only.
4. Wait for confirmation, then refresh the balance, shortfall, and activation state.

Read current thresholds instead of hardcoding Ethereum or non-L1 minima. The management service supports activation exemptions; `is_active: true` with a positive shortfall does not establish that execution gas is funded or PPS is current.

Upkeep withdrawal follows proposal and execution. Check the pending withdrawal, effective time, and recipient; inspect the resulting balance after execution. Removing upkeep can change activation and discovery and must be reviewed against continuing obligations to depositors.

## Fund execution gas

Before activation, verify the configured executor/submitting account, native token, chain, balance, and expected transaction costs with the deployment owner. Account mode and sponsorship configuration can change which account pays. These docs do not provide a universal funding address or a universal gas threshold.

Monitor the actual execution account's native balance and rejected submissions. If gas is low, fund the verified account through the approved treasury process, then confirm the credited balance. Do not retry a failing production intent merely to test the top-up; inspect its existing state before any resubmission.

## Distinguish funding failures

| Symptom | Check |
|---|---|
| Positive upkeep shortfall | Required UP threshold, balance, exemption policy, and pending withdrawal |
| Session ready but submission fails | Native gas, payer/account mode, transaction error, nonce, and service availability |
| True rule but no publication | Freshness, positive integer size, cooldown, concurrency, pause, and kill-switch gates |
| Repayment or redemption cannot complete | Input token units, available idle funds, source exit liquidity, and remaining debt |
| Unknown balance or stale response | Treat as unknown; refresh the authoritative source before declaring readiness |

See [Launch checklist](/operate/ui/setup-checklist), [Monitoring](/operate/automation/monitoring), and [Fund redemption requests](/operate/playbooks/redemptions). Upkeep, gas, and cash-reserve controls must each have an owner and an alert path.

---

# Vault Settings
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate/ui/vault-settings

Vault Settings is the configuration hub for vault-level controls. Most settings use the same pattern: Erebor prepares calldata, the manager wallet signs, and the protocol contract applies the change onchain.

Public SuperVault detail pages expose Vault Settings as read-only context. Manager-only controls, including upkeep deposit/withdrawal and settings transactions, remain in the authenticated Operate flow.

<Note>
Prepare endpoints return transaction data. They do not mutate protocol state by themselves. The connected wallet must sign and submit the transaction.
</Note>

## Access Model

Erebor settings writes for fees, deviation threshold, PPS expiration, banned leaves, and redemption timing require the Primary Manager. For minimum update interval, proposal and cancellation are Primary-Manager-only, but either manager can prepare execution. The Aggregator permits any caller to execute a valid pending interval proposal after its timelock expires. A narrower UI control does not change that contract authority. Notification-channel operations permit either manager. Preparing calldata is not authorization to sign as another account.

See [Permissions Model](/operate/permissions) for the full matrix.

## Fees

Configure the vault's performance fee, management fee, and fee recipient.

Fee changes protect depositors through the protocol's proposal/timelock rules. The dashboard displays current values and prepares the required transaction when a primary manager proposes a change.

## PPS Parameters

Price-per-share controls define how often PPS can update and when stale data blocks operations.

Common fields:

- **Deviation threshold** — maximum allowed difference between calculated and current PPS.
- **PPS expiration / staleness** — when vault operations should stop waiting for a fresh PPS update.
- **Minimum update interval** — minimum time between PPS updates.

These settings are read from vault detail data and changed through signed transactions.

## Redeem Timelock

Redeem timelock is an offchain keeper timing setting. The management service stores the configured delay; it is not a new onchain lock or a guarantee of liquidity at expiry.

Relevant APIs:

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/v1/redeem-timelocks` | GET | List configured timelocks |
| `/api/v1/redeem-timelocks/bulk` | PUT | Bulk set offchain timelocks |
| `/api/v1/vaults/{chain_id}/{vault_address}/redeem-timelock` | GET | Read one vault's timelock |
| `/api/v1/settings/redeem-timelock` | GET/PUT/DELETE | Read, store, or remove the offchain setting |

<Warning>
Do not infer how existing requests will be processed from a successful settings write. Review pending requests, effective keeper policy, and liquidity before changing the delay; read the stored value back afterward.
</Warning>

## Banned Hook Leaves

A banned hook leaf is blocked even if it appears in an authorized merkle tree. Use this to quickly stop a specific hook + parameter combination while you prepare a cleaner merkle config update.

Banning a leaf is narrow: it blocks the exact leaf, not the entire hook category.

## Upkeep and Activation

UP upkeep funds the upkeep system and contributes to vault activation. It does not fund native-chain execution gas. See [Upkeep and gas funding](/operate/ui/funding).

The Upkeep panel shows:

- Current upkeep balance.
- Upkeep token.
- Required balance and shortfall.
- Activation status: `active` or `insufficient_upkeep`.
- Whether the vault is active for keeper operations and discoverable in public listing surfaces.
- Pending upkeep withdrawal proposal, if any.

Erebor computes activation from threshold sufficiency or an activation exemption. An active flag can coexist with a positive shortfall; inspect both rather than assuming every operational gate is clear. Responses separate `upkeep_info`, `activation`, and upkeep `withdrawal_status`.

### Deposit Upkeep

Managers deposit upkeep through the settings flow:

```bash
POST /api/v1/settings/upkeep/deposit
```

The dashboard handles token allowance checks first, then prepares the deposit transaction for wallet signature.

### Withdraw Upkeep

Withdrawals use a propose / execute pattern:

```bash
POST /api/v1/settings/upkeep/withdraw/propose
POST /api/v1/settings/upkeep/withdraw/execute
```

Use withdrawals carefully on live vaults. Pulling the balance below threshold can make the vault inactive or undiscoverable.

## Session Keys

Session keys delegate limited execution authority for automation. They are used by the OMS / Strategy Engine path so strategies can publish and execute intents without asking the manager wallet for every tick.

Erebor exposes vault-scoped session-key inventory and prepare endpoints:

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/v1/session-keys` | GET | List session keys visible to the manager |
| `/api/v1/vaults/{chain_id}/{vault_address}/session-key` | GET | Read a vault session key |
| `/api/v1/vaults/session-key/prepare` | POST | Prepare grant transaction |
| `/api/v1/vaults/session-key/revoke/prepare` | POST | Prepare revoke transaction |

OMS also exposes strategy-automation session-key readiness and rotation endpoints. Follow [Execution accounts and session keys](/operate/ui/execution-accounts); do not infer execution readiness from a session inventory row alone.

## Notification Channels

Notification channels attach Slack, webhook, or websocket destinations to a vault.

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/v1/notification-channels` | GET/POST | List or create manager-owned channels |
| `/api/v1/vaults/{chain_id}/{vault_address}/notification-channels` | GET | List vault channels |
| `/api/v1/vaults/{chain_id}/{vault_address}/notification-channels/{channel_id}` | POST | Attach channel |
| `/api/v1/vaults/{chain_id}/{vault_address}/notification-channels/{channel_id}` | DELETE | Detach channel |

Use notification channels for operational alerts. They are not a guaranteed durable integration event stream; see [Notifications and audit polling](/operate/automation/webhooks).

## Alert Delivery

Alerts connect vault events to notification destinations. Treat alert delivery as operational plumbing: create the channel first, bind it to the vault, then verify delivery with a low-risk event before relying on it for incidents.

Notification channel records include:

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `provider` | Channel provider or transport. |
| `name` | Operator-facing channel name. |
| `config` | Provider-specific destination config. Sensitive values should be redacted in UI. |
| `created_by` | Creator metadata. |
| `created_at` / `updated_at` | Audit timestamps. |

Recommended alert categories:

- Upkeep shortfall or activation loss.
- PPS staleness.
- Failed keeper runs.
- Session-key readiness changes.
- Emergency pause / unpause.
- Emergency liquidity exit arm / stop.
- Merkle generation or publish failure.
- Repeated OMS execution failure.

Troubleshooting:

| Symptom | Check |
|---------|-------|
| Channel exists but receives nothing | Confirm it is bound to the vault. |
| Sensitive destination appears in UI | Redact config display and rotate the destination if leaked. |
| Alerts are noisy | Tune event thresholds before muting the channel. |
| Incident alert is missing | Check audit logs and notification-channel binding first. |

## API Reference

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/v1/vaults/{chain_id}/{vault_address}` | GET | Full vault detail including fee, PPS, and upkeep data |
| `/api/v1/settings/fee-config` | GET | Read current fee config |
| `/api/v1/settings/fee-config/propose` | POST | Prepare fee-config proposal transaction |
| `/api/v1/settings/fee-config/execute` | POST | Prepare fee-config execution transaction |
| `/api/v1/settings/deviation-threshold` | GET | Read PPS deviation threshold |
| `/api/v1/settings/deviation-threshold/update` | POST | Prepare deviation-threshold update transaction |
| `/api/v1/settings/pps-expiration` | GET | Read PPS expiration / staleness setting |
| `/api/v1/settings/pps-expiration/propose` | POST | Prepare PPS-expiration proposal transaction |
| `/api/v1/settings/pps-expiration/execute` | POST | Prepare PPS-expiration execution transaction |
| `/api/v1/settings/pps-expiration/cancel` | POST | Prepare PPS-expiration cancellation transaction |
| `/api/v1/settings/redeem-timelock` | GET/PUT/DELETE | Read, update, or remove redeem timelock |
| `/api/v1/settings/banned-hook-leaves` | GET | Read banned hook leaves |
| `/api/v1/settings/banned-hook-leaves/update` | POST | Prepare banned-hook-leaf update transaction |
| `/api/v1/settings/min-update-interval` | GET | Read minimum PPS update interval |
| `/api/v1/settings/min-update-interval/propose` | POST | Prepare min-update-interval proposal transaction |
| `/api/v1/settings/min-update-interval/execute` | POST | Prepare min-update-interval execution transaction |
| `/api/v1/settings/min-update-interval/cancel` | POST | Prepare min-update-interval cancellation transaction |
| `/api/v1/settings/upkeep` | GET | Read upkeep state |
| `/api/v1/settings/upkeep/deposit` | POST | Prepare upkeep deposit |
| `/api/v1/settings/upkeep/withdraw/propose` | POST | Prepare upkeep withdrawal proposal |
| `/api/v1/settings/upkeep/withdraw/execute` | POST | Prepare upkeep withdrawal execution |
