# User management
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate/ui/user-management

## Select the vault

Open **User Management** in authenticated Operate and verify chain, vault address, and connected wallet. The public Roles tab is read-only. Session authentication does not itself grant access to a vault.

| Action | Required management role | Change type |
|---|---|---|
| Add/remove Secondary Manager | Primary Manager | Prepared onchain transaction |
| Add/remove view-only user | Primary or Secondary Manager | Offchain assignment |
| Update user display name | Primary or Secondary Manager | Offchain metadata |
| Replace Primary Manager | Separate contract recovery/governance path | Not an ordinary edit in this tab |

## Secondary Managers

Choose **Add Secondary Manager**, enter the verified wallet address, and prepare the transaction. Inspect chain, strategy, target wallet, and decoded operation before signing. For removal, prepare and sign the removal transaction. After confirmation, read the manager list and onchain membership again.

A Secondary Manager has delegated operational powers, not unrestricted access to primary-only settings. Removing a manager is not the same as revoking every session that may have been granted previously; review [Execution accounts](/operate/ui/execution-accounts) during an access change.

## View-only users and display names

Either manager can add or remove an offchain view-only assignment. The assigned user must authenticate to inspect private rules. View-only users cannot save, start, or simulate strategies.

Display names help identify wallets but are not authority. Verify addresses independently before granting access; read the assignment back after each change.

## Primary Manager

The Primary Manager tab displays the current main manager. The Aggregator supports a `SUPER_GOVERNOR` replacement path and a separate Secondary-Manager-initiated timelocked proposal path. It is not immutable or governance-only. Review [Access and roles](/operate/permissions) and the current contract state before an approved recovery procedure.

## Management API contracts

These upstream paths are mediated by the browser BFF; they are not standalone credential instructions.

| Method | Path | Operation |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/users` | List users, scoped by `chain_id` and `vault_address`; paginate the result |
| POST | `/api/v1/users/secondary-manager/prepare` | Prepare add-manager transaction |
| POST | `/api/v1/users/secondary-manager/remove/prepare` | Prepare remove-manager transaction |
| POST | `/api/v1/users/view-only` | Add view-only assignment |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/view-only/{wallet}` | Remove assignment with vault/chain context |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/users/{wallet}/display-name` | Update offchain name with vault/chain context |

If a role change appears stale, refresh the user session and selected-vault data. Do not retry grants until the transaction receipt and current membership have been checked.

---

# Strategy canvas
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate/ui/strategy

## Read the canvas

| Visible lane | Actions | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Deposit | `DEPOSIT` | Deploy into a source |
| Redemption | `WITHDRAWAL`, `CLAIM` | Redeem or claim source assets |
| Rebalance | `REBALANCE`, `SWAP`, `BRIDGE`, `CLAIM_REWARDS` | Other supported movements and reward claims |

A strategy card describes a rule and action definition. Its lifecycle state, permission to edit it, and in-flight execution are different properties. RUNNING means eligible for evaluation, not proof of a successful transaction. IDLE or CREATED definitions remain visible without being active policy.

Public vault routes provide read-only strategy context and activity. Authenticated inspection depends on `canInspect`; mutation depends on `canManage` and operational gates. A public card is not a guarantee that its rule editor opens. Do not interpret a disabled edit or toggle control as an engine failure.

## Create and edit

1. Select the intended chain and vault.
2. Use **Add deposit strategy**, the redemption add control, or a rebalance add control for the intended action.
3. Select a yield source and registry-backed hook. Review its parameters and execution steps.
4. Add the boolean rule and numeric size separately. Inspect copied engine expressions, especially decimal normalization.
5. Review conviction, slippage, duration, cooldown, and concurrency.
6. Save, then reopen and compare the returned ID, version, state, rules, and plan.

Follow [Build your first strategy](/operate/strategy/quickstart) for an inactive-save exercise. **Create** and save are real configuration writes, not expression tests. Starting is a separate state change. Updates require the current version; reload and reconcile a `409 Conflict`.

The editor's quantity/type validation and metadata checks do not execute an arbitrary supplied snapshot. There is no verified dedicated **Test expression** button in this surface.

## Inspect a definition

Record the strategy ID and version before comparing behavior. Review:

- Exact source, oracle, position binding, and first-hook denomination.
- Rule tree, including guards and exact threshold boundaries.
- Numeric size, caps, and output propagation between steps.
- Whether indicators are configured and ready.
- Stored lifecycle versus kill switch, emergency target locks, and executor readiness.

[Variables and units](/operate/strategy/variables), [Rules and expressions](/operate/strategy/dsl), and [Sizing and plans](/operate/strategy/action-config) define those contracts without relying on visual shorthand.

## Order and locks

Drag within a lane to change server-managed priority. The reorder request must include every non-archived strategy in that lane exactly once. Lower numeric priority is preferred in the relevant signal group; visual order does not sequence transactions across cards.

A target-scoped emergency lock blocks publication for affected USER_DEFINED strategies and disables their related controls. Other targets can remain operable. The special `EMERGENCY_EXIT` strategy is controlled from [Pause Operations](/operate/ui/pause), not the normal editor.

A missing or expired execution session key can block automation even when a strategy is RUNNING. Upkeep, gas, hook authorization, source freshness, and liquidity are separate checks. See [Lifecycle, priority, and concurrency](/operate/strategy/lifecycle).

## Inspect activity

Open a strategy's activity in **Intent History**, then filter by vault and strategy. Follow intent ID → execution ID → fill → transaction hash. Rule evaluation alone is not a fill, and Intent History does not record every false tick. Use the [worked AP1 investigation](/operate/ui/intent-history) to distinguish recorded completion from an economically reconciled position.

## Source boundary

Labels and controls are reviewed against [UI b782f60](https://github.com/superform-xyz/monorepo/tree/b782f601be8c29b5258fc9a2ed02f71209ee5c37/apps/superman/src/domains/strategy), including the panel/card access gates and `useStrategyRuleBuilderState.ts`. Authenticated editing and signing were not rehearsed for this documentation release.

---

# Build your first strategy
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate/strategy/quickstart

## Choose a prepared vault

Use a dedicated vault you are authorized to manage, with a configured yield source, supported deposit hook, pricing, and execution account. Complete the [launch checklist](/operate/ui/setup-checklist) first. Do not edit a running production strategy for this exercise.

Deposit only when idle exceeds 10% of vault assets, then leave 7.5% idle. The vault underlying and deposit hook's input asset must match. This is not a USDC deposit recipe for an NVDA-denominated vault.

## Author the definition

1. In **Strategy**, choose **Add deposit strategy**. Name it `Reserve deposit - inactive exercise` and select the prepared yield source and its asset-consuming deposit hook. Leave indicators empty.
2. Wait for underlying decimals and hook parameters to resolve. Check the **Size expression** denomination is the vault underlying, not source shares. **Literal** shows raw state values; **Formatted** shows decoded values. Changing this display toggle does not rewrite an existing expression.
3. In **Rule tree**, paste only `vault_tvl > 0 AND vault_free_assets > 0.10 * vault_tvl`. Use the editor's `AND` gate, **not `&&`**, and do not paste JSON. Copy returns the expression; the saved `rules` tree should be:

```json
{
  "type": "AND",
  "children": [
    {"type": "EXPR", "expr": "vault_tvl > 0"},
    {"type": "EXPR", "expr": "vault_free_assets > 0.10 * vault_tvl"}
  ]
}
```

4. Paste this complete raw-unit expression into **Size expression**, rather than entering individual human-amount chips:

```text
max(vault_free_assets - 75 * vault_tvl / 1000, 0)
```

Both inputs are raw underlying units; `75 / 1000` encodes the 7.5% target without a decimal-literal multiplication at the tested integer boundary. The VM still uses finite-precision arithmetic and intent sizing truncates, so test raw-unit boundaries. Unlike depositing all idle assets, this preserves the reserve. The first hook must consume assets, not shares. Let the registry-backed editor supply the hook, source, oracle, and `execution_params.plan.steps`; inspect the [plan shape](/operate/strategy/action-config).

5. Use **Copy** on Size expression. For this full-expression paste, expected normalized `action_config.size_expr` is `max ( vault_free_assets - 75 * vault_tvl / 1000 , 0 )`. Clipboard input is canonical DSL: the editor must not multiply this already-raw size by token decimals. Hand-entered human-value chips and explicitly decoded variable chips can compile differently; a decoded six-decimal variable compiles as `( variable / 1e6 )`. If the copied result differs beyond whitespace, stop and retest that result rather than assuming display equivalence.
6. Under **Signal & risk**, select **BINARY** in **Conviction** and enter **60** in **Cooldown (s)**. The payload contains `conviction_config.mode: "BINARY"` and `cooldown_ms: 60000`. There is **no editable concurrency control** in this editor: create/update payloads set `max_concurrent: 1`.
7. Set **Max slippage (bps)** and **Signal lifespan** for the selected venue, including a positive slippage budget on a budget-consuming plan. These controls are not a vault-wide balance lock.

## Check expected behavior

These synthetic cases were run through the actual engine compiler/evaluator. Assume a six-decimal underlying and unchanged total assets during the modeled deposit.

| Total assets, raw | Idle, raw | Trigger | Truncated deposit, raw | Idle after modeled deposit |
|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| `100000000` | `20000000` | true | `12500000` | `7500000` |
| `100000000` | `10000000` | false | no intent | unchanged |
| `100000000` | `10000001` | true | `2500001` | `7500000` |
| `0` | `0` | false | no intent | unchanged |
| missing | missing | false in isolated evaluator | no intent | unknown in production |

Post-action evaluation at 7.5% is false. Fees, prices, other strategies, and settlement can change the actual reserve; verify it rather than assuming the model is a fill.

There is no verified arbitrary-snapshot **Test** button in this editor. Editor validation, local evaluator tests, [model simulation](/operate/ui/simulation), transaction preflight, and mined results are different evidence.

## Save without starting

Choose **Create**, then reopen the saved definition. Confirm:

- New strategy ID and version, with the intended chain and vault.
- State `CREATED` or `IDLE`, **not `RUNNING`**.
- Copied engine rule and size match the tested expressions, including decimal normalization.
- Action `DEPOSIT` and a first plan step that consumes underlying assets.
- Correct target, execution account, hook parameters, slippage, cooldown, and concurrency.

Saving is a real configuration write; starting is separate. If the returned state is unexpectedly RUNNING, stop and investigate. Updates carry a version; on `409 Conflict`, reload and compare before resubmitting.

## Activation review

Leave this exercise inactive. For an approved rollout, review freshness, session keys, hook authorization, upkeep, execution gas, source liquidity, and competing strategies. Select the saved strategy explicitly when simulating; supported simulations load inactive definitions into RUNNING in memory without starting production automation.

After separately approved activation, follow [Intent History](/operate/ui/intent-history), then verify the reserve. Add a separate refill strategy only after checking the [reserve playbook](/operate/playbooks/reserves).

<Note>
The authoring flow is source-reviewed at [UI b782f60](https://github.com/superform-xyz/monorepo/tree/b782f601be8c29b5258fc9a2ed02f71209ee5c37/apps/superman/src/domains/strategy). Authenticated create/readback and activation were not rehearsed for these documentation tests.
</Note>

---

# Variables and units
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate/strategy/variables

## Inspect values before writing a rule

The engine evaluates raw snapshot numbers. Authorized shard-state responses expose `fields` as `{raw, scale}`; human display is `raw × 10^-scale`. A display conversion does not change expression input units. The editor's Copy operation emits the normalized engine expression, which can include decimal divisors.

Use the editor's variable catalog and authorized shard state for the selected vault. Upstream routes are `GET /api/v1/indicators/catalog` and `GET /api/v1/engine/shards/{vault_id}/state`; these are not promises of anonymous access. The OS browser uses the session-mediated Strategy BFF. Public definitions reveal aliases, but not necessarily their current values. Historical intent snapshots are not live balances.

Vault IDs use chain ID, an underscore, and vault address. The [dated carry example](/operate/playbooks/carry#captured-configuration) supplies the superNVDA mapping. Do not reuse its position ID for another Spoke, reserve pair, owner, or chain.

## Field catalog

Patterns below are descriptive, not executable aliases. Addresses in aliases are lowercase `0x` plus 40 hex characters; position IDs are `0x` plus 64 lowercase hex characters. Supported yield-source identities can also be 32-byte market IDs where the provider supplies them.

| Field / pattern | Source and quantity | Engine units and display |
|---|---|---|
| `vault_free_assets` | Underlying-token balance at the strategy | Raw underlying units; underlying decimals |
| `vault_tvl` | Engine accounting from total supply × PPS | Underlying asset base units, **not USD TVL** |
| `vault_total_supply` | Vault accounting | Raw vault shares; share decimals |
| `vault_pps` | Vault PPS feed | Fixed-point PPS; use returned scale, not source-PPS assumptions |
| `vault_redeem_queue_count` | Redemption queue | Integer request count |
| `vault_redeem_queue_value` | Pending redemption accounting | Raw underlying units, comparable to `vault_free_assets` |
| `vault_inflight_request_count` | Outstanding async requests | Integer count |
| `token_<address>_amount` | ERC-20 `balanceOf(strategy)` | Raw token units; token decimals |
| `native_amount` | Native strategy balance | Raw native units; chain-native decimals |
| `token_<address>_price_usd` | Token quote provider | Human USD price, scale zero |
| `position_<id>_collateral_<token>_amount` | Normalized lending position | Raw collateral-token units |
| `position_<id>_debt_<token>_amount` | Normalized lending position | Raw debt-token units |
| `position_<id>_risk_collateral_value_e18` | Venue risk adapter | Risk-reference value scaled by `1e18` |
| `position_<id>_risk_debt_value_e18` | Same position and risk convention | Risk-reference value scaled by `1e18` |
| `position_<id>_borrow_capacity_e18` | Venue capacity adapter | Risk-reference value scaled by `1e18` |
| `position_<id>_liquidation_capacity_e18` | Venue liquidation adapter | Risk-reference value scaled by `1e18` |
| `position_<id>_capacity_used_bps` | Venue adapter | Basis points; `10000` represents full capacity |
| `position_<id>_health_factor_e18` | Optional venue metric | Dimensionless ratio scaled by `1e18` |
| `position_<id>_borrow_rate_e18`, `_supply_rate_e18` | Optional pricing-provider rates | Integer ratio scaled by `1e18`; period/APR-vs-APY is **not carried by this schema**; see rate boundary below |
| `ys_<identity>_amount` | Source allocation converted to assets | Raw source-underlying units |
| `ys_<identity>_shares` | Source share balance | Raw source shares |
| `ys_<identity>_pps` | Source price provider | Human assets per share, scale zero |
| `ys_<identity>_liquidity` | Exit-liquidity observation | Raw source-underlying units |
| `ys_<identity>_liquidity_shares` | Exit-liquidity observation | Raw withdrawable shares |
| `ys_<identity>_inflight_request_count` | Source async tracking | Integer count |
| `ys_<identity>_apy`, `_base_apy`, `_reward_apy` | Analytics opportunity `apy`, `baseApy`, `rewardApy` | Scale-zero annual percentage points in the analytics/model contract: `5` means 5%, not `0.05`; upstream convention must match |
| `ys_<identity>_tvl` | Analytics opportunity `tvl` | Provider's scale-zero TVL, not raw vault-underlying liquidity; currency metadata is not returned with this field |
| `price`, `underlying_price` | Configured price feed/context | Scale-zero quote; establish quote currency and source, do not infer either from the alias |
| `volume`, `days_to_maturity` | Track input / configured maturity | Volume retains producer units (no universal period); maturity is fractional days until `maturity_unix` in seconds, evaluated with millisecond tick time |
| `tick_unix`, `tick_unix_ms` | Evaluation clock | Seconds and milliseconds; wire scale of milliseconds is 3 |
| `tick_hour`, `tick_minute`, `tick_second`, `tick_dow`, `tick_day`, `tick_month`, `tick_year` | UTC evaluation clock | Integer calendar components; Sunday is day-of-week zero |
| Configured indicator alias | Indicator DAG over a selected track | Units depend on indicator and track; warmup required |

## Real carry aliases

<Accordion title="Exact production identifiers, captured 2026-10-19">

| Quantity | Exact alias |
|---|---|
| Idle USDC | `token_0x833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913_amount` |
| USDC debt | `position_0xacaa6ee9de7631b927242d42fb8c256860545fa457560f550b653a925bc6cb3b_debt_0x833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913_amount` |
| Collateral risk value | `position_0xacaa6ee9de7631b927242d42fb8c256860545fa457560f550b653a925bc6cb3b_risk_collateral_value_e18` |
| Debt risk value | `position_0xacaa6ee9de7631b927242d42fb8c256860545fa457560f550b653a925bc6cb3b_risk_debt_value_e18` |
| NVDAc collateral | `position_0xacaa6ee9de7631b927242d42fb8c256860545fa457560f550b653a925bc6cb3b_collateral_0xb20000000000000000000078ee7ce2fe4908108c_amount` |
| Clearstar shares | `ys_0x91c056b6d4311a743614fbc03ac32d4e6a2d3a3c_shares` |
| Clearstar assets | `ys_0x91c056b6d4311a743614fbc03ac32d4e6a2d3a3c_amount` |
| Clearstar PPS | `ys_0x91c056b6d4311a743614fbc03ac32d4e6a2d3a3c_pps` |
| Asset exit liquidity | `ys_0x91c056b6d4311a743614fbc03ac32d4e6a2d3a3c_liquidity` |
| Share exit liquidity | `ys_0x91c056b6d4311a743614fbc03ac32d4e6a2d3a3c_liquidity_shares` |

</Accordion>

Debt and collateral values are comparable within the same provider's risk-reference convention. Their ratio is LTV; neither is a token amount. Do not assume every reference value is USD. `vault_free_assets` in this NVDAc-denominated vault is not idle USDC.

## Asset/share conversion

For human PPS `P`, asset decimals `a`, and share decimals `s`:

- Asset raw → share raw: `asset_raw × 10^(s-a) / P`.
- Share raw → asset raw: `share_raw × P / 10^(s-a)`.

Clearstar uses 18-decimal shares and six-decimal USDC, so the factor is `10^(18-6) = 1e12`. With synthetic PPS 1.25, two USDC (`2000000` raw) converts to `1600000000000000000` raw shares:

```text
2000000 * 1e12 / 1.25
```

This factor is specific to that pair. Intent sizing truncates toward zero. A redemption hook consumes shares; a repayment hook consumes debt tokens. Use metadata and [plan effects](/operate/strategy/action-config), not a universal “size is assets” assumption.

## Rate and analytics conventions

- **Analytics APY:** `ys_0x91c056b6d4311a743614fbc03ac32d4e6a2d3a3c_apy` is the concrete alias shape for the case-study source; its presence/value must be checked, not inferred from the source's existence. The adapter copies opportunity `apy`, `baseApy`, and `rewardApy` without conversion. The model explicitly interprets APY as **annual percentage points** and accrues `amount × (APY / 100) × elapsed / year`; it is not evidence of a provider's compounding methodology. Do not add reward APY to an `apy` that already includes rewards. The current-opportunity schema has no lookback or provider observation timestamp. Its historical fallback can copy an old APY/TVL point into a newly timestamped feed update. An updated shard is therefore **not proof of current yield**.
- **Position rates:** for example, `position_0xacaa6ee9de7631b927242d42fb8c256860545fa457560f550b653a925bc6cb3b_borrow_rate_e18` has display scale 18. Raw `50000000000000000` displays as ratio `0.05`; it means 5% **only for the provider's stated period**, not necessarily annual APY. The position client parses upstream `borrow_rate`/`supply_rate` integer strings without annualizing. Neither position response nor engine alias encodes rate period, compounding, or APR/APY type. Omitted optional rates stay absent, not verified zero. No live Aave V4 rate-period contract was established by this capture.
- **Resolve the provider boundary before a spread rule:** inspect the authorized position row's `provider`, `protocol_address`, `market_label`, reserve bindings, and `observed_at`. Ask the pricing/feed operator for that exact provider/reserve's rate definition (period, APR or APY, scale, observation block) and the analytics operator for the matched opportunity's `source`, `chain`, `address`, base/reward inclusion, lookback, observation time, and TVL currency. Compare like annualized notionals only after those records agree. If those metadata are unavailable, leave spread-dependent entry inactive; do not guess a multiplier or substitute the dashboard APY.

## Availability, freshness, and inspection

Use **Strategy → the selected definition → variable/state inspection** under an authorized browser session. The upstream shard route above returns `fields`, `positions`, `yield_source_allocations`, `yield_source_liquidity`, and per-strategy `last_eval_at`/`last_signal`. It does **not** expose a universal per-field timestamp, feed-ready flag, or indicator-ready endpoint. A current `last_eval_at` is evaluation time, not the age of every input.

| Family | What the curator can inspect | Availability / freshness boundary and concrete next check |
|---|---|---|
| Vault PPS, supply, total assets, free assets and queue | Exact aliases in `fields`; raw/scale; pending requests and underlying balance via authorized reads | Internal `TrackedField.UpdatedAt` and feed-cycle readiness are not serialized in `fields`. Obtain the subgraph/queue poll timestamp and indexed block from the engine/feed operator when freshness matters; compare onchain state at a named block. Missing evaluator fields can look like zero. |
| Token/native balances | `token_0x833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913_amount`, `native_amount`; compare strategy `balanceOf`/native balance at a named block | Token RPC failure retains the last-known value. Field presence is not a successful latest poll. Ask for token/native feed last successful poll and failure status; do not treat a missing field as an empty wallet. |
| Position amounts, risk, capacity, health and rates | `positions[]`: `position_id`, `provider`, `protocol_address`, token `amount`/`decimals`, `block_number`, `block_hash`, `observed_at`, optional `stale`/`retired`, and optional rate/health values | All belong to a pinned-block generation. An incomplete poll retains prior data and marks it stale; optional omissions remain absent. Compare block/observation and require non-stale matching identity. Ask the position-feed operator for configured maximum age if it is not visible. A retired zero position is not an active zero-debt loan. |
| Source allocation assets/shares | `fields` and `yield_source_allocations[]`; Clearstar `_amount`/`_shares` above | Raw source assets/shares, not USD. Allocation rows omit zero-valued optional properties, so inspect `fields` plus source contract balances. Poll provenance is not exposed in the allocation row; obtain balance-feed block/time before sizing. |
| Source PPS | Clearstar `_pps` in `fields`; source/oracle selection in the plan | FairPrice ingest uses producer `observed_at` and optional `valid_until`, plus configured `FairPriceMaxAge`; receipt time is not source age. Missing/future/expired observations fail admission. These PPS provenance fields are **not forwarded by this shard allocation projection**: ask the feed operator for the matched FairPrice observation/deadline and configured age bound. Zero is never a valid divisor. |
| Asset/share exit liquidity | `yield_source_liquidity[]`: `address`, `asset_address`, `status`, `shares_status`, `collected_at`, `valid_until`, `shares_valid_until`; values in `_liquidity` and `_liquidity_shares` | Inspect asset and share status separately. Missing asset decimals can prevent asset liquidity even when a share observation exists. Require usable, unexpired observations for the exact source/asset; never substitute TVL. |
| APY/base/reward APY and analytics TVL | `yield_source_allocations[]` and corresponding `fields` aliases | Zero properties may be omitted; analytics defaults and absence are not proof of zero yield. Ask for the matched opportunity/history timestamp and source conventions above. Feed-cycle readiness does not reject an old historical APY merely because it is old. |
| Token/market prices | `token_0x833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913_price_usd` for USD quotes; `price` for the configured market track | Positive quotes and configured observation-age checks are required. Price provenance is not attached to every shard field. Obtain the provider observation time and configured quote maximum age from the price-feed operator. Do not infer market hours or price freshness from chain activity. |
| Volume / maturity | Selected indicator `params.field`, `maturity_unix`, configured tick inputs | Volume has no universal currency, interval, or availability guarantee; require the producer's contract. Maturity uses Unix seconds and floors remaining days at zero. Missing required track input is not a ready zero series. |
| In-flight counts | `vault_inflight_request_count`, source count, and shard tracked/occupying intent counts; verify actual OMS/source requests | Counts are derived workload, not amounts or guaranteed arrival. Inspect request ID, phase, claimability and last event time for settlement readiness. |
| Indicators | Saved `indicators` configuration, catalog outputs, dependency fields and historical intent snapshot when present | Internal `Ready()` gates evaluation; no universal ready boolean is exposed by this shard response. Ask the engine operator for warmup/root-input diagnostics using strategy ID/version and alias. Zero output does not establish readiness. |
| Clock | `tick_unix`, `tick_unix_ms`, UTC calendar fields | Evaluation clock, not feed freshness; no `tick_age_seconds` alias. |

Referenced dependencies must have been observed and satisfy the configured feed warmup. Positions, PPS, liquidity and price quotes add their own freshness checks; this is **not a uniform maximum-age guarantee for every balance or analytics field**. `risk_params.eval_max_staleness_ms` checks evaluation age, not upstream observation age. If the authorized response omits the provenance needed for a consequential decision, obtain it from the named feed operator; do not extract browser credentials or invent an inspection API.

## Reusable calculations

The inspected backend persists `indicators: [{name, params, alias}]`, rules, and size expressions. `StrategyConfig` does not expose a generic persisted `custom_variables` expression map. Use registered indicator aliases with catalog parameters, or repeat an explicit subexpression. Shorthand such as `D`, `C`, or `repay_needed` is not executable unless it is an actual configured output.

Derived expressions and indicator outputs are not durable “keep unwinding” state. A threshold becoming false stops a stateless rule even if debt remains.

### Verified indicator serialization

The engine's `TestDeriveRequiredSnapshotKeys_IndicatorAliasUsesRootPPS` configures this indicator: `{"name":"sma","alias":"smooth_pps","params":{"window_ms":1000,"field":"ys_0xe8dd6a1e13244a27bdaa19ccbf33013647c675d1_pps"}}`. It is an **actual source-test configuration**, not a claim that the dated NVDAc strategies use indicators (their captured arrays are empty). Store it as an entry in `indicators`, not in a `custom_variables` map. In the editor select the catalog's `sma`, its `field`, a `window_ms` of `1000`, and alias `smooth_pps`; the field must resolve for the selected vault before authoring against it.

`smooth_pps` is the executable single-output alias; the test's rule is `smooth_pps > 0.9`. The value is the sample mean of the human PPS track, so it remains assets per share, not a token amount or annual yield. A one-second window is milliseconds, **not one sample**: readiness requires at least two retained samples and window coverage (including the implementation's aged-out anchor). The engine follows the indicator's root PPS dependency for freshness; an indicator alias does not bypass PPS admission. Multi-output indicators use `alias_output` such as MACD's `_histogram`, and chained parameters use `from` plus the catalog's `from_output` rather than inventing an expression variable.

Indicator tracks use float64. Do not use a smoothed raw 18-decimal balance as an exact integer sizing substitute; values above `2^53` can lose precision. Inspect catalog outputs, saved parameters, and root-feed evidence, then test the actual graph's warmup and rule before activation.

## Source boundary

Naming and scale are pinned to [Strategy Engine fc50b3c](https://github.com/superform-xyz/superman-strategy/tree/fc50b3ca5f1d66294e7476b1ff1088e92b126fbd/internal/domain), especially `eval_field.go`, `position_eval.go`, `balance_eval.go`, and `eval_state_keys.go`. Source inspection and synthetic fixtures do not establish freshness of a live position.

---

# Rules and expressions
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate/strategy/dsl

## Rule trees

Each strategy has one boolean `rules` tree. Action sizing is a separate numeric expression.

| Node | Required fields | Evaluation |
|---|---|---|
| `EXPR` | `expr` | Boolean expression, not numeric truthiness |
| `AND` | `children`, at least two | All pass; short-circuits in order |
| `OR` | `children`, at least two | Any passes; short-circuits in order |
| `NOT` | `children`, exactly one | Negates that child |
| `VOTE` | `children`, `threshold` | Requires `ceil(threshold × child count)` passes |

`VOTE.threshold` is a fraction greater than zero and at most one. The following tree requires two of three children, not one:

```json
{
  "type": "VOTE",
  "threshold": 0.5,
  "children": [
    {"type": "EXPR", "expr": "true"},
    {"type": "EXPR", "expr": "false"},
    {"type": "EXPR", "expr": "true"}
  ]
}
```

`NOT` has no singular `child` field:

```json
{"type": "NOT", "children": [{"type": "EXPR", "expr": "false"}]}
```

## Expression grammar

| Operation | Syntax |
|---|---|
| Arithmetic | `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, parentheses, scientific notation such as `1e12` |
| Comparison | `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `==`, `!=` |
| Boolean | `&&`, `||`, `!`, `true`, `false` |
| Numeric functions | `min(a, b)`, `max(a, b)`, `abs(a)`, `clamp01(a)` |

`min` and `max` take exactly two arguments. Nest them for additional caps. There is no `floor`, `pow`, ternary operator, assignment, or arbitrary JavaScript execution.

```text
min(3, max(1, 2))
```

The result is `2`. Numbers use the engine's high-precision expression VM. Positive action sizes are truncated toward zero when converted to integer intent amounts; a positive fraction below one raw unit does not create a usable amount. See [Sizing and execution plans](/operate/strategy/action-config).

## Guard runtime division

Prefer multiplication for ratio triggers:

```json
{
  "type": "EXPR",
  "expr": "vault_tvl > 0 && vault_free_assets > 0.10 * vault_tvl"
}
```

If division is necessary, place its guard first:

```json
{
  "type": "EXPR",
  "expr": "vault_tvl > 0 && vault_free_assets / vault_tvl > 0.10"
}
```

Both are false for an empty snapshot without dividing by zero. `AND`/`OR` tree order matters for the same reason. Do not rely on a guard in a different strategy. A `VOTE` tree is not a substitute for an outer safety guard.

## Validation stages

1. **Editor:** quantity, token metadata, action parameters, and expression checks help construct a payload. Copy the normalized engine expression to inspect its actual units.
2. **Save:** backend shape, identifier-policy, and static-type checks reject malformed trees, unknown aliases, and boolean/numeric type mismatches. This is not an empty-snapshot execution.
3. **Evaluation:** the compiled expression reads a snapshot. Missing identifiers read as zero at this low-level stage; division can still fail at runtime.
4. **Publication:** readiness, freshness, positive integer size, conviction, risk, cooldown, and occupied-slot checks can prevent an intent even when its boolean rule is true.
5. **Execution:** authorization, available balances, venue constraints, slippage, and transaction success are separate checks.

A syntactically valid dynamic identifier is not proof that a feed supplies it. Use [Variables and units](/operate/strategy/variables), not invented aliases such as `vault_pps_stale`, `tick_age_seconds`, or `ys_<address>_alloc`.

## Conviction

```json
{"mode": "BINARY"}
```

| Mode | Current-evaluation score |
|---|---|
| `BINARY` | One when the rule fires, zero otherwise |
| `RULE_VOTE_RATIO` | Fraction of passing top-level children |
| `INDICATOR_DISTANCE` | Absolute indicator distance divided by configured scale, clamped to the allowed range |
| `EXPR` | Numeric expression clamped to `[0, 1]` |

Minimum conviction can suppress publication. These modes do **not** count consecutive passing ticks. `RULE_VOTE_RATIO` evaluates top-level children independently, so a separate top-level guard does not protect another child's division while calculating that score. Make each child safe or use `BINARY` for a guarded trigger.

## Source boundary

Grammar, validation, and evaluation are pinned to [Strategy Engine fc50b3c](https://github.com/superform-xyz/superman-strategy/tree/fc50b3ca5f1d66294e7476b1ff1088e92b126fbd/internal/rule), including `compiler.go`, `evaluator.go`, and `identpolicy.go`. Local evaluator fixtures verify these examples; they do not establish deployed binary parity or transaction execution.

---

# Sizing and execution plans
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate/strategy/action-config

## Three decisions

1. `rules` decides whether the strategy is eligible.
2. `action_config.size_expr` produces the first action's positive integer input amount.
3. `execution_params.plan.steps` describes hook order, effects, parameters, and amount propagation.

A true trigger does not fix a wrong denomination. A positive size does not prove sufficient balance, authorization, or liquidity.

## Action fields

| Field | Contract |
|---|---|
| `action` | Directional enum such as `DEPOSIT`, `WITHDRAWAL`, or `REBALANCE` |
| `size_expr` | Numeric expression converted to integer raw input units |
| `objective` | `BALANCED`, `MIN_SLIPPAGE`, or `MIN_TIME` routing objective |
| `from_address` | Vault/account context; not necessarily the token-holding strategy contract |
| `target_address`, `target_type` | Target and canonical family such as `ERC4626` or `VAULT` |
| `execution_params.strategy_address` | Strategy execution contract |
| `execution_params.plan.steps` | Ordered registry-selected hook metadata and arguments |
| `max_slippage_bps` | End-to-end slippage budget; positive when a plan consumes one |
| `max_duration_seconds` | Deadline policy; deferred plans have additional duration requirements |

Legacy top-level `execution_name` and `execution_address` are not the current plan contract. Generate hooks and arguments with the registry-backed editor. Do not invent addresses or mix encoded arguments with a different source/oracle.

## Input denominations

| Hook pattern | First input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| Approve + deposit ERC-4626 | Raw underlying assets | Received source shares |
| Redeem ERC-4626 | Raw source shares | Received underlying assets |
| Aave V4 borrow | Raw debt-token amount | Received debt tokens |
| Aave V4 repay | Raw debt-token amount | Spent amount / debt reduction, not redeemed vault shares |

The VM returns a high-precision number. Intent construction truncates toward zero, rejects non-positive/infinite values, and rejects positive fractions that become zero. Adding `1` means one **raw** unit of the current denomination, not one human token.

## Borrow then deposit

This complete `action_config` was captured on 2026-10-19 from the **IDLE** fixed-amount strategy in the [carry case study](/operate/playbooks/carry#captured-configuration). It passes the pinned engine's plan validation. It is a read-only example, not a creation request or activation recommendation.

## Redeem then repay

This plan fragment is AP1's captured `execution_params`. Its first input is raw Clearstar shares; repayment consumes actual assets produced by redemption. Retrieve the matching rules and `size_expr` from the [dated configuration read](/operate/playbooks/carry#captured-configuration), and review the [guard and sizing explanation](/operate/playbooks/deleverage#redeem-assets-to-repay). Do not pair it with the borrow example's amount or the simplified idle-repayment size.

</Accordion>

These plans have immediate `EXECUTE` steps on the same chain and vault, intended as a bundled hook transaction. The historical AP1 record has one `hook_tx` fill. Do not generalize that to every route: deferred, bridged, or asynchronous actions can require separate transactions and settlement phases. Canvas order is not a dependency scheduler.

## Sizing and verification

For a target repayment, apply `(debt value - target × collateral value) / debt value` to the raw debt amount, then cap by available funds. For redeem → repay, convert the desired assets to shares using PPS and the decimal difference, then cap by held shares and observed asset/share exit liquidity.

AP1's `0.99` liquidity cushion, `1.001` repayment buffer, and `0.9998` slippage factor are distinct controls. A liquidity cap can leave the target unmet. See [Variables and units](/operate/strategy/variables#assetshare-conversion).

Before publication, inspect freshness, input/output units, hook authorization, slippage, balances, session keys, and gas. After a fill, reconcile source shares, debt-token receipts, debt reduction, and residual tokens. Schema validation is not a transaction preflight or economic proof.

Source: [engine action/plan validation](https://github.com/superform-xyz/superman-strategy/tree/fc50b3ca5f1d66294e7476b1ff1088e92b126fbd/internal/domain) and [OMS hook adapter](https://github.com/superform-xyz/superman-oms/tree/bf36ed9fb23a640c34943544f824ff4f5fb77939/internal/execution/adapters/hook_tx). No production writes or fork execution were performed.

# Lifecycle, priority, and concurrency
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate/strategy/lifecycle

## Stored lifecycle

| From | Allowed next states |
|---|---|
| `CREATED` | `IDLE`, `RUNNING` |
| `IDLE` | `RUNNING`, `ARCHIVED` |
| `RUNNING` | `IDLE`, `ERROR` |
| `ERROR` | `IDLE` |
| `ARCHIVED` | None |

Only RUNNING strategies tick. Stop a running strategy to IDLE before archiving; RUNNING → ARCHIVED is not a direct transition. A kill switch can block intent issuance without changing the stored RUNNING state.

Configuration updates and state changes use optimistic concurrency. Read the latest version before changing a definition. A stale-version conflict is a request to reconcile changes, not to retry the same payload indefinitely.

## Publication gates

A true rule is only one input to publication. Check feed readiness and indicator warmup, freshness of referenced position/PPS/liquidity/token-price data, positive integer size, conviction, risk limits, cooldown, occupied slots, kill switches, and target emergency locks.

Intent History records published intent activity, not every false evaluation. An empty history does not tell you which gate blocked a strategy.

## Priority is not a transaction scheduler

Lower numeric priority is preferred within the engine's relevant signal group. Aggregation groups by chain, evaluation identity, and action, with deterministic tie breakers. Dragging cards changes priority in a lane; it does not create an execution dependency between cards.

The reorder operation submits every non-archived strategy in the selected lane exactly once. Priorities are server-managed rather than set by create/update payloads. Read back the order after a change.

Use a supported [execution plan](/operate/strategy/action-config) when a second hook must consume a first hook's result. Do not express borrow → deposit as two cards and assume their canvas order makes them atomic.

## Cooldown and occupying slots

`cooldown_ms` starts after **successful publication**, not after a fill or false evaluation. `60000` means sixty seconds. Terminal failure does not bypass an active cooldown or the other publication gates.

`max_concurrent: 1` limits occupying intents for **one strategy**. Another strategy can still compete for the same idle token or collateral. Vault-level risk/concurrency controls are separate. Some asynchronous workflows release an occupying slot before their full settlement lifecycle finishes; inspect outstanding requests as well as the slot count.

Signal epochs track direction and meaningful conviction changes. A published intent suppresses duplicate submissions while it occupies the current epoch. Terminal outcomes clear tracking/suppression; restart rehydration restores concurrency rather than stale epoch suppression. Do not build a durable unwind latch from these mechanics.

## Pause and recovery

Stopping a strategy prevents future evaluations. It does not repay debt, redeem source shares, remove collateral, or cancel every already-published intent. Before restarting, reconcile in-flight intents and actual balances. Otherwise a new evaluation can act on a state that is about to change.

USER_DEFINED high-LTV rules are different from `EMERGENCY_EXIT`, which has special target locks and emergency handling. Use [Pause and recovery](/operate/ui/pause) for those controls and [Deleverage and unwind](/operate/playbooks/deleverage) for economic position reduction.

## Source boundary

Verified against [Strategy Engine fc50b3c](https://github.com/superform-xyz/superman-strategy/tree/fc50b3ca5f1d66294e7476b1ff1088e92b126fbd/internal/engine), `domain/strategy.go`, `shard_tick.go`, `shard_execute.go`, `aggregator.go`, and `intentprojection.go`. Tests cover cooldown, an occupied strategy slot, and stale-version conflict; no production state transitions were performed.

# Testing and simulation
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate/ui/simulation

## Coverage before running

| Mechanism | Establishes | Does not establish |
|---|---|---|
| Editor checks | Expression/quantity structure, required parameters, metadata readiness | Behavior on arbitrary snapshots or transaction success |
| Backend save validation | Rule shape, allowed identifiers, static types, plan schema | Empty-snapshot execution or usable live data |
| Actual evaluator fixtures | Rule and size behavior for supplied synthetic snapshots | Production freshness gates, balances, permissions, or fills |
| Backtest / Look Ahead | Commands and modeled outcomes for supported inputs and selected definitions | A forked transaction or forecast of returns |
| Separately authorized transaction preflight | Transaction feasibility under the chosen state/model | Future settlement or future liquidity |
| Mined receipt and position reconciliation | What a particular execution actually changed | Success of future executions |

## Current carry support

The [2026-10-19 superNVDA definitions](/operate/playbooks/carry#captured-configuration) were checked against the pinned simulator admission validator:

| Definition / input | Admission | Economic coverage |
|---|---|---|
| AP0 / AF0 idle-USDC repayment | Admitted | No implemented Aave repayment feedback proving post-action LTV |
| AP1 / AF2 redeem → repay | Rejected | Referenced asset/share liquidity is unsupported by replay |
| Source allocation deposit/withdrawal | Model has allocation feedback | Synthetic outcomes, not venue execution |
| REBALANCE action | No allocation delta from the publisher model | Not a loan-position transition |
| Look Ahead token balances/prices | Seeded at initialization | Not automatically evolved as a complete debt/collateral market |

The exact AP1/AF2 admission error contains:

```text
liquidity observations are not supported by simulation replay
```

<Warning>
Do not remove production liquidity guards to make a strategy simulate. AP0/AF0 admission is not proof that repayment, debt reduction, liquidation safety, or target LTV has been modeled.
</Warning>

## Run a supported model

1. Open **Simulation** with the intended vault selected.
2. Choose **Backtest** with **From** / **To**, or **Look Ahead** with **Horizon (hours)** and **Seed Price (optional)**. A blank seed uses live price where available.
3. Select only the intended persisted strategy IDs. The UI initially selects loaded strategies; review this rather than assuming isolation.
4. Inspect **Execution Model**: **Fill Ratio**, **Slippage (bps)**, **Reject Prob**, **Fail Prob**, **Min Latency (ms)**, and **Max Latency (ms)**.
5. Choose **Run Backtest** or **Run Forward Simulation**. Running requires manager write authority in the inspected UI.
6. Review charts, **Simulation Outcomes**, per-strategy breakdowns, and **Commands**. Compare exact trigger boundaries and integer amounts, not only totals.

Requests select persisted `strategy_ids`; they do not accept an arbitrary unsaved rule and snapshot. The backend loads selected CREATED/IDLE configurations into RUNNING in memory for the simulation, without updating their production lifecycle. Do not start a live strategy merely to make it selectable.

Backtests depend on available history, source coverage, and model seeding. PPS fallback seeding can be used when history is absent. Record the data window and assumptions alongside the result. Zero commands is not itself proof of either correctness or failure.

## Saved results and caching

Name the result and choose **Save Simulation** to retain it; **Discard** clears the current result. If a matching run exists, the UI says **Existing simulation found. Running will load cached results.** and offers **Load Existing Result**. That is not a fresh computation.

When comparing an edit, retain strategy IDs/versions, rules, sizes, selected scope, input range, execution-model settings, and whether the result was cached. A saved result is evidence for that configuration and model, not the current live vault.

## Evaluator test matrix

Before activation, test at least:

- Normal state and exact trigger boundaries.
- Missing inputs, zero debt/collateral, zero PPS, and zero exit liquidity.
- Insufficient idle funds, one-raw-unit dust, and positive fractions truncated to zero.
- Asset/share conversion and the intended post-action reserve or LTV.
- A partial unwind that disarms while debt remains.
- Cooldown, occupied concurrency slot, and stale-version update.
- Unsupported simulation inputs without deleting their guards.

Local documentation fixtures invoke the actual pinned engine compiler/evaluator and plan validator. They are not a browser test endpoint. See [Troubleshooting](/operate/strategy/troubleshooting) when a strategy saves but does not publish or settle.

## Source boundary

Reviewed [Strategy Engine fc50b3c](https://github.com/superform-xyz/superman-strategy/tree/fc50b3ca5f1d66294e7476b1ff1088e92b126fbd/internal/sim): `strategy_validation.go`, `publisher.go`, and `internal/api/sim_util.go`; [UI b782f60](https://github.com/superform-xyz/monorepo/tree/b782f601be8c29b5258fc9a2ed02f71209ee5c37/apps/superman/src/domains/simulation). No authenticated deployed simulation, production execution, or forked transaction was performed for this release.

---

# Strategy anti-patterns
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate/strategy/anti-patterns

| Anti-pattern | Why it fails | Better design |
|---|---|---|
| Deposit every idle asset while claiming a reserve target | Sizing contradicts the stated objective | Deposit only excess above the target |
| Treat `vault_tvl` as USD or `vault_free_assets` as USDC in every vault | Engine accounting uses the vault underlying | Match the token and raw scale explicitly |
| Treat every `size_expr` as assets | Redeem hooks can consume shares | Inspect first-step effects and convert with actual decimals/PPS |
| Reuse first-hook share count for repayment | Repayment consumes debt tokens | Chain actual redemption output with `use_prev_hook_amount` |
| Assume save validation dry-runs zero inputs | Validation is static | Test zero/missing snapshots with the evaluator |
| Guard division in a different strategy or unsafe VOTE child | No cross-strategy short-circuit; vote/conviction can evaluate children independently | Keep denominator guards in the evaluated expression path |
| Set VOTE threshold to a count | The backend expects a fraction in `(0, 1]` | Use the desired passing fraction and test the rounded requirement |
| Treat conviction as consecutive passing ticks | Modes score the current evaluation | Use verified temporal indicators/policy if persistence is needed |
| Copy a dynamic alias and assume data exists | Shape validation does not prove feed availability | Inspect field, scale, provider, freshness, and readiness |
| Remove exit-liquidity guards to make replay run | Simulation coverage is narrower than production dependencies | Preserve the guard and report unsupported replay |
| Treat `max_concurrent: 1` as a portfolio lock | It applies to one strategy | Review shared-balance competition and vault-level controls |
| Treat card order as an atomic workflow | Priority is not a transaction dependency scheduler | Use a supported execution plan for dependent hooks |
| Call a liquidity-capped repayment a guaranteed target | Available resources can be insufficient | Measure the resulting debt and LTV |
| Call a high-LTV rule a persistent full unwind | Once the threshold is false, it stops | Track residual debt and the approved exit objective explicitly |
| Call pause an unwind | Pausing does not repay, redeem, or release collateral | Separate control scope from economic recovery |
| Treat COMPLETED or aggregate output as a reconciled outcome | Projection fields can be incomplete | Decode receipts and compare positions |
| Default missing service telemetry to success | Unknown becomes falsely healthy | Emit an explicit unknown condition |
| Retry a stale-version update unchanged | It overwrites or conflicts with newer intent | Reload, compare, and submit a reviewed update |

## A counterexample worth testing

A stateless rule triggers at 55% LTV and requests full repayment capped by available liquidity. If a partial fill moves LTV from 56% to 51%, the rule stops while debt remains. Neither the phrase “full unwind” nor a one-intent concurrency setting changes that behavior.

The [deleverage playbook](/operate/playbooks/deleverage) tests this case. The [reserve playbook](/operate/playbooks/reserves) tests resulting-state invariants rather than only whether a rule passes. Use [Troubleshooting](/operate/strategy/troubleshooting) to identify the failing stage before modifying production policy.

---

# Manage an idle reserve
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate/playbooks/reserves

## Define the reserve objective

For a single-source vault whose underlying matches the source asset:

- Deposit when idle assets exceed 10% of total assets.
- Refill when idle assets fall below 5%.
- Size either action toward a 7.5% idle target.

The gap between triggers prevents immediate direction reversal around the target. It is not a promise that prices, fees, or concurrent actions cannot move the reserve outside the band.

`vault_tvl`, `vault_free_assets`, and `vault_redeem_queue_value` use vault-underlying base units. `vault_tvl` is not the dashboard's USD TVL. For a multi-asset carry vault, idle debt tokens need their own `token_<address>_amount` alias.

## Deposit excess only

```json
{"type": "EXPR", "expr": "vault_tvl > 0 && vault_free_assets > 0.10 * vault_tvl"}
```

```text
max(vault_free_assets - 75 * vault_tvl / 1000, 0)
```

Use a deposit hook that consumes raw underlying assets. With synthetic total assets `100000000` and idle `20000000`, the expression deposits `12500000` and leaves `7500000`. The resulting trigger is false. Depositing all idle funds would contradict the reserve objective.

## Refill the shortfall

```json
{"type": "EXPR", "expr": "vault_tvl > 0 && vault_free_assets < 0.05 * vault_tvl"}
```

The raw-asset shortfall is:

```text
max(75 * vault_tvl / 1000 - vault_free_assets, 0)
```

This is an **asset budget**, not a share-consuming redemption size. Cap an asset-consuming withdrawal by available allocation and observed exit liquidity. For a share-consuming redemption, convert the capped budget with the actual asset/share decimals and positive PPS, then cap by held and liquid shares.

For the separately identified Clearstar/USDC source, this executable expression demonstrates the available-share cap:

```text
min(ys_0x91c056b6d4311a743614fbc03ac32d4e6a2d3a3c_shares, min(0.99 * ys_0x91c056b6d4311a743614fbc03ac32d4e6a2d3a3c_liquidity_shares, 0.99 * ys_0x91c056b6d4311a743614fbc03ac32d4e6a2d3a3c_liquidity * 1e12 / ys_0x91c056b6d4311a743614fbc03ac32d4e6a2d3a3c_pps))
```

Evaluate the cap only after a positive-PPS guard. The `0.99` cushion is a case-study choice, not a universal requirement.

### Complete same-asset refill

Use a **prepared USDC-underlying vault** with Clearstar cbAssets configured as a source. This is a synthetic same-asset exercise, **not the superNVDA deployment**: both the vault shortfall and source liquidity below are six-decimal USDC. Source shares are 18 decimals. In **Add redemption strategy**, select that source and `Redeem4626VaultHook`, with `owner` equal to that vault's execution strategy contract. Do not append a repayment hook: the USDC must remain at the strategy for reserves or fulfillment.

The following are engine wire examples; in Rule tree use `AND` gates for the conjunctions, then compare the saved definition. Require positive source observations as well as the reserve trigger:

```json
{"type":"EXPR","expr":"vault_tvl > 0 && vault_free_assets < 0.05 * vault_tvl && ys_0x91c056b6d4311a743614fbc03ac32d4e6a2d3a3c_pps > 0 && ys_0x91c056b6d4311a743614fbc03ac32d4e6a2d3a3c_shares >= 1 && ys_0x91c056b6d4311a743614fbc03ac32d4e6a2d3a3c_liquidity >= 1 && ys_0x91c056b6d4311a743614fbc03ac32d4e6a2d3a3c_liquidity_shares >= 1"}
```

Size in raw source shares, taking the smaller of the converted shortfall and each exit cap:

```text
min(max(75 * vault_tvl / 1000 - vault_free_assets, 0) * 1e12 / ys_0x91c056b6d4311a743614fbc03ac32d4e6a2d3a3c_pps, min(ys_0x91c056b6d4311a743614fbc03ac32d4e6a2d3a3c_shares, min(99 * ys_0x91c056b6d4311a743614fbc03ac32d4e6a2d3a3c_liquidity_shares / 100, 99 * ys_0x91c056b6d4311a743614fbc03ac32d4e6a2d3a3c_liquidity * 1e12 / (100 * ys_0x91c056b6d4311a743614fbc03ac32d4e6a2d3a3c_pps))))
```

With total assets `100000000`, idle `4000000`, PPS `1.25`, held shares `80000000000000000000`, liquid shares `80000000000000000000`, and asset liquidity `100000000`, the requested size is `2800000000000000000` shares. At unchanged PPS and no execution loss it returns `3500000` raw USDC, leaving `7500000` idle; both reserve triggers are then false. With asset liquidity limited to `2000000`, size is capped at `1584000000000000000` shares, modeled receipt is `1980000` USDC raw, and idle reaches only `5980000`. That is below target but above the refill trigger: this band does **not** automatically finish refilling to 7.5%.

Save inactive; inspect the first step's `SHARES → ASSETS` effect and the strategy recipient before any approved activation. Stop on unresolved decimals, zero/stale PPS, zero liquidity, sub-unit truncated size, or an unsettled prior withdrawal. Slippage and fees can leave less than the modeled amount; reconcile actual share burns and USDC receipts, then evaluate the band again. An async source requires a different request/claim plan and is not covered by this immediate ERC-4626 example.

## Boundary and resulting-state checks

| Synthetic state | Expected result |
|---|---|
| Idle exactly 10% | No deposit |
| Idle exactly 5% | No refill |
| Idle 4 of total 100 | Asset shortfall 3.5; modeled refill leaves 7.5 |
| Idle 7.5 of total 100 | Neither trigger passes |
| Total assets zero or unavailable | Neither guarded rule passes in isolated evaluation |
| Exit liquidity zero | No usable refill; alert rather than assume the target was reached |
| PPS zero | Guard must block share conversion |
| Positive size below one raw unit | Integer sizing cannot publish a usable amount |

After each real execution, inspect the underlying balance and new accounting snapshot. A liquidity-limited refill can leave the reserve below 5%; outstanding async requests can also mean funds are not yet spendable.

## Coordinate withdrawals and other strategies

Reserve deployment must not compete blindly with [redemption funding](/operate/playbooks/redemptions). Review queued obligations before depositing excess, and avoid overlapping definitions that independently spend the same balance. `max_concurrent: 1` applies per strategy, not per asset or portfolio.

Use the [inactive first-strategy exercise](/operate/strategy/quickstart), then separately review the refill plan and [simulation support](/operate/ui/simulation). A source-liquidity expression can be valid in production and unsupported by model replay.

---

# Run a borrow-and-carry strategy
Source: https://docs.superform.xyz/operate/playbooks/carry

## Position model

A borrow-and-carry vault supplies collateral to a lending venue, borrows a debt token, and deposits that token into a yield source. The resulting assets and liabilities are different positions:

| Position | Accounting question |
|---|---|
| Collateral token in the lending venue | How much can safely be released after debt changes? |
| Debt token owed | What principal, accrued interest, and risk-reference value remain? |
| Yield-source shares | How many shares are held and what assets can be realized now? |
| Idle collateral and debt tokens | Which token is available at the strategy contract? |
| Depositor redemption obligations | Which underlying token must return to the vault? |

Lending income minus borrowing cost is the base carry spread. Compare rates over the same period and notional; include fees, slippage, idle balances, and execution costs. Incentives are a separate component, not evidence the base spread is positive. Collateral price performance is not carry income.

## Bind the inputs

Before authoring, select chain, strategy owner, lending venue/Spoke, supply and borrow reserves, collateral token, debt token, source, oracle, and normalized position ID. Confirm the source's share and asset decimals separately. Inspect the current field values and observation freshness through your authorized session.

Offchain rules, onchain hook permissions, venue solvency constraints, and operating policy are different enforcement layers. A rule describing an LTV target does not turn that target into an onchain invariant.

## Entry and idle reserves

Set the intended collateral allocation, borrow limit, idle-token reserve, and minimum acceptable carry spread explicitly. A supported borrow → deposit plan can pass received debt tokens to the deposit step. Two separately ordered canvas cards do not create that transaction dependency.

Do not use vault-underlying idle assets as debt-token liquidity when the tokens differ. For superNVDA, idle USDC is `token_0x833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913_amount`; the vault's free underlying is NVDAc.

Separate the **entry gate**, **repayment trigger**, **repayment sizing target**, and **hard venue threshold**. The last must come from the actual position/venue configuration. A 55% automation trigger is not itself the venue's liquidation boundary.

## Captured configuration

The following is a **2026-10-19 configuration snapshot**, not universal SuperStocks policy or a claim about current balances. Public strategy enumeration returned 27 definitions: six RUNNING, seventeen IDLE, and four CREATED. Refresh the public definitions before using this case study operationally:

```bash
curl --fail-with-body --get \
  'https://os.superform.xyz/api/strategy/api/v1/strategies' \
  --data-urlencode 'vault_id=8453_0xc441a2cc3a528b6312740448a70cc4d40f4d7bfc' \
  --data-urlencode 'kind=USER_DEFINED' \
  --data-urlencode 'state=CREATED' \
  --data-urlencode 'state=IDLE' \
  --data-urlencode 'state=RUNNING' \
  --data-urlencode 'state=ERROR' \
  --data-urlencode 'limit=50' --data-urlencode 'offset=0'
```

If the response total exceeds the returned page, continue pagination; a limit-one query cannot establish portfolio policy. Public reads do not authorize writes or expose all live shard values.

| Definition | ID | Version / captured state | Economic role |
|---|---|---|---|

| Borrow fixed amount and deposit | `5d3e2a1b-8f5a-4f68-b1a4-ce0e6069a2ad` | IDLE | Example plan, not active entry policy |

| MW manual collateral release | `4f7bcb58-e86d-4983-922b-fc3b0b9920a7` | IDLE | Not an automatically completed exit |
| Q3 / Q4 queue-funding profiles | `161c658a-5466-48a6-8fc3-fd3d51e91d71` / `1cf1fc20-46a1-4703-8eff-45702ae32cfc` | CREATED | Not running queue-funding policy |

AP0/AP1 trigger at `52% <= LTV < 55%` and size toward 50%. AF0/AF2 trigger at `LTV >= 55%` and attempt full debt repayment, capped by resources. All four were USER_DEFINED, BINARY, with sixty-second cooldown, one concurrent intent per strategy, two-basis-point slippage, and sixty-second maximum duration. The 50% target is **not** a global vault entry target; the other RUNNING definitions retain their 40% gates.

## Worked entry decision

Inspect **Deposit USDC in cbAssets**, ID `556d695e-bf66-4cdc-863a-5542c67a305e`, captured version 14 / RUNNING. This is the deployment leg of carry, not a borrowing command. Its actual rule requires positive idle USDC and either (a) both debt amount and risk debt value equal zero, or (b) positive debt amount, positive debt/collateral risk values, and debt risk value **strictly below 40%** of collateral risk value. Its size is the entire idle-USDC alias; it does not retain a USDC reserve or test a rate spread.

| Synthetic observation / decision | Result under the captured definition |
|---|---|
| Idle `10000000` raw USDC; debt `39000000` raw USDC; risk debt `39000000000000000000`; risk collateral `100000000000000000000` | Rule true; request `10000000` raw USDC |
| Same observations but risk debt exactly `40000000000000000000` | Rule false at the strict 40% boundary |
| Positive idle, both debt amount and risk debt value zero | Debt-free branch true; still requires fresh position/balance data |
| Debt amount zero but risk debt value positive | Neither branch true; investigate inconsistent observations |

The single `ApproveAndDeposit4626VaultHook` consumes USDC from execution strategy `0xef83abc641b98af01f0652e3af49a25d65c601a5` and receives Clearstar shares. At synthetic PPS `1.25`, no fees/loss, and the first row's input, expected new shares are `8000000000000000000` raw, idle USDC becomes zero, and the next trigger is false. Debt and collateral are unchanged by this deposit. Verify the actual receipt, share delta, and debt after execution; a modeled share amount is not a quote or fill.

**Operator decision:** if your mandate requires an idle-USDC reserve or minimum spread, this captured definition is not sufficient even when its rule is true. Leave a proposed replacement inactive until those explicit conditions and its capped size have been reviewed. Do not represent the capture's 40% gate as a 50% target.

The captured **Borrow fixed amount and deposit** draft (`5d3e2a1b-8f5a-4f68-b1a4-ce0e6069a2ad`, version 46 / IDLE) is more limited: its only rule is positive `borrow_capacity_e18`; size is `10000000000` raw USDC (10,000 USDC). The [two-step plan](/operate/strategy/action-config#borrow-then-deposit) passes actual borrowed USDC into Clearstar. A positive capacity observation does **not** prove capacity for that fixed amount: do not activate it as a complete entry policy. Review current venue capacity, proposed post-borrow risk, rate period/spread, and a deliberate idle policy before approving any borrowing. The draft supplies a supported plan shape, not evidence of active or bounded borrowing.

## Exit and withdrawal pressure

Use idle debt tokens first where the rule permits. If none are available, source redemption must be capped by held shares, asset liquidity, share liquidity, PPS, and slippage. The captured split is one raw USDC unit: even dust can select the idle branch rather than the source branch.

Debt repayment does not release collateral automatically. To fund NVDAc redemptions, first reduce debt as needed, then release collateral under venue constraints and return the required underlying. A USDC source redemption that immediately repays debt has not yet funded an NVDAc redemption queue. See [Deleverage and unwind](/operate/playbooks/deleverage) and [Fund redemption requests](/operate/playbooks/redemptions).

## SuperStocks checks

- Read token precision from metadata. Do not assume all stock, debt, and share tokens have the same decimals.
- Identify the actual market/risk oracle and its update policy. These source-oracle addresses do not by themselves establish freshness of the underlying stock price.
- Account for market gaps, price jumps, issuer/transfer restrictions where applicable, and venue liquidity. A continuous blockchain does not make every underlying market continuously liquid.
- A desired market-closed borrowing guard is not evidence such a guard exists in the captured rules. Verify explicit conditions rather than inferring policy from product names.

## Controlled activation and monitoring

Save new definitions inactive and read them back. Test exact boundaries and units with the evaluator. Review [simulation limitations](/operate/ui/simulation) before treating any model as validation. Activate only within an approved rollout after reviewing permissions, gas, upkeep, session keys, freshness, and conflicting strategies.

Monitor collateral/debt value, debt amount, rate spread, idle USDC, source shares/PPS, exit liquidity, queue pressure, publication failures, and actual post-execution deltas. Missing telemetry is unknown, not healthy. Pause new borrowing when required by your approved policy; pausing automation does not unwind outstanding debt.

## Evidence boundary

Configuration was captured through public GETs. Engine behavior is reviewed at [fc50b3c](https://github.com/superform-xyz/superman-strategy/tree/fc50b3ca5f1d66294e7476b1ff1088e92b126fbd); plans at [OMS bf36ed9](https://github.com/superform-xyz/superman-oms/tree/bf36ed9fb23a640c34943544f824ff4f5fb77939). This is not deployed-binary verification, live position measurement, or authenticated activation rehearsal.
